tieu_de: Preface
noi_dung:
Foreword

The teachings of the saints, although they say that they are largely the same, the Buddha's teachings are truly superior. There is no need to consider the profound meaning, just the fact that the Buddha established the precept of not killing can definitely confirm that he is a saint of saints, no one can compare.

As humans, whether wise or foolish, everyone considers being killed to be the greatest suffering, but being kept alive is the greatest virtue. Therefore, in terms of the heaviest crime, there is nothing more than the crime of killing, but the greatest blessing is nothing more than preventing killing.

All animals are greedy for life and afraid of death, looking for a safe place, avoiding harm, no different from human psychology! Yet, the words referring to the killing of animals for food and drink are found mixed up in Confucian scriptures and storybooks, causing people to become familiar with it after reading it, and then take it for granted that this is the case.

If there were no Great Hero1 to take pity on sentient beings and first establish strict precepts and strict instructions, who would know the meaning of "all sentient beings have spiritual nature, all living things are of the same nature"?

NOTE 1

Dai Hung: one of the revered names for Buddha. He is revered as Great Hero, Great Power, Great Compassion.

Nowadays, Confucians also talk about loving animals, but I don't understand things like cutting, chopping... how can it be said to be loving? The Book of Confucianism teaches that: “Cutting down a tree, killing an animal at the wrong time is unfilial.” 2 But they really don't know that peace and harmony always exists, that in this universe there is no suitable time for killing! Whenever there are droughts or floods, the court also knows to prohibit slaughter in the hope of touching heaven's heart, but in normal times, it indulges in encouraging killing, harming the peace of heaven and earth, sowing the seeds of disaster, just leaving it alone without saying anything. I really don't know how to understand that?

NOTE 2

This sentence is taken from the Confucian book of Rites (禮記). Original text: 斷一樹， 殺一獸，不以其时，非孝也。 - One life to end, one beast to kill, no matter the time, no filial piety."

In the Sutras it is taught that:3 “Once the Holy King of Chakravarti appears in the world, he immediately gives orders everywhere, stopping killing, so that all people in the land can enjoy blessings

NOTE 3

This content is based on chapter ten dedication, Avatamsaka Sutra.

happy, long life, never even hearing words like war, hunger."

We are unfortunately born in impure times, the world's morality is increasingly deteriorating, the ancestors and saints saw that the tendency to kill living beings was too heavy, it was difficult to change, so they reluctantly taught that “you should not kill too much”. But then those words were passed down through books, and could not help but be relied on by greedy mortals to satisfy their desires, [thinking that if killing was not too much, it would be acceptable]. Saying it out loud makes people unable to hold back their pity.

My friend Mr. Chu An Si felt sorry for the world so he wrote this book to awaken people's conscience, hoping to change the long-standing trend of killing. He compiled this book, collected and selected it, explained it clearly, presented it with all his heart, with great diligence and painstaking effort, and mentioned what he had seen and known from far and wide, used it to destroy the old and stubborn theories of Confucianism, only hoping that when people read it, they would immediately wake up from their long dreams, and their serious illness would immediately be cured. Indeed, this book can be seen as a shining light in today's cruel and greedy world.

Like-minded people should encourage each other to engrave copies of [this book] and print them for circulation. Always remember that not killing is the first of the precepts, and kindness is the basis of all goodness.

Those are the things the saints and sages have mercifully and clearly taught, so the book's name is “Van Thien Tien Tu”, which means “the first foundation of ten thousand good things”.

You should know that wherever this book is present, it will certainly be protected by countless sages and saints using righteous concentration and compassion. All the gods and demons will respectfully surround it and use all kinds of incense and flowers to sprinkle that place as offerings.

Compatriot, scholar in Ngu Van

Truong Lap Liem, alias Bang Am1

NOTE 1

Layman Truong Lap Liem (张立廉) was born in 1620, lived in During the Qing Dynasty, his personal name was Hong Nhat (鸿一), his name was Bang Am (冰庵), he passed the Bachelor's degree exam in the 9th year of Chong Trinh (1636), he was a person who studied widely and was profound in the classics.

Respectfully

tieu_de: It is recommended to read this book
noi_dung:
BOOK ONE

ADVICE
ON CAUSE AND EFFECT SUPER PART

Recommendations for reading this book1

NOTE 1

This chapter covers the most essential points of the prevention of killing (Author's Note)

Kindness comes first Normally,2 the virtue of kindness is the first among all virtues. How great is the treatise of the Three Teachings, although 3 uses different words, it says the same thing: "Everyone loves their life to live, all living things want to survive."

NOTE 2

The Five Eternals: according to Confucianism are benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom and faith.

NOTE 3

Only Confucianism, Taoism and Buddhism.

When the chicken saw the cook coming to catch him, he panicked and flew high to avoid it. When the pig heard the butcher cut the price to buy it, two streams of tears flowed out like streams. They all know that death is coming, just because their mouths cannot speak. Suddenly having to endure the agony of being chopped up by knives and chopping boards, the intestines being cut into pieces when life is still

never completely ended, sharp knives cut thousands of times, boiling water boiled and cooked hundreds of times. Bringing the bodies of all creatures into the boiling oil and fire, then using them as delicious and strange dishes on your dining table. If doing something like that is innocent, is there anything to fear from heaven? In the past, those who killed had to endure a cycle of retribution without fail.

Ever since I was just an adult, seeing [scenes of killing] gave me great compassion, so I immediately collected and arranged old stories [advising killing], and now there are a lot of them. I have made a vow to save the suffering of the Three Paths,1 to keep my aspirations stronger day by day, [so I wrote these stories to circulate and advise people]. When I put down the pen, my heart felt even more sympathetic, each word was choked up. [When I finished writing] I wanted to engrave a print, but the poor didn't have enough strength and donating wasn't easy, so I had to stagnate for the past three or four years, and now I've finished printing it for circulation.

NOTE 1

Refers to the three evil paths, i.e. the realms: hell, hungry ghosts, and animals.

I would like to respectfully advise all knowledgeable sages to pay attention and read this book.

Listen to the advice of God. live2

NOTE 2

Excerpted from Mong Giac Thien (夢覺篇). (Author's note.)

Manh Trieu Tuong is a native of Giao Ha,3 in the year of the Rat in the 40th year of Van Lich, he participated in the Huong4 exam and passed the exam. Suddenly got sick with pain

NOTE 3

Belongs to Hebei province.

NOTE 4

That is in 1612.

spleen, dreamed of going to the underworld, met the King of Hell and said: “Mr. You have great blessings and a long life, just because killing too many lives is a sin, now it will be deducted from your blessings. If from now on you know how to keep the precepts and not kill anymore, but do the work of releasing lives, and tell the words you heard in this dream to advise people [to do good], then you can atone for that sin."

Manh Trieu Tuong agreed and promised to do so, but woke up and forgot and did nothing. One night, I had the same dream again, and I was extremely scared. At that time, when he failed to pass the exam, he immediately returned to his hometown to fulfill his promise. That very night, the house where Manh Trieu Tuong lived [in the capital] had its main beam broken, and the bed he had previously slept in was crushed into dust.

Manh Trieu Tuong immediately wrote down this incident and printed it into the book Meng Giac Thien (夢覺篇) to advise people to do good and avoid evil. Later, he passed the doctorate exam and became a mandarin.

COMMENT

All people in life are accustomed to following the old ways, hesitant and timid and immersed in mistakes all their lives. If Mr. Manh Trieu Tuong had had the slightest hesitation or timidity at that time, he would have been ruined, so how could he still enjoy blessings later? Therefore, the book Dream of Heaven in which he recounts his life story can truly help others wake up from their dreams.

The Lord of Hell obeys good deeds1

NOTE 1

Excerpt from Touch Thien Quang So (感應篇廣疏). (Editor's note.)

Trinh Khue from Tien Duong,2 was once sick, and dreamed that the deceased3 bachelor, Luc Dung Thanh, came to visit him, and the attendant was even more solemn than when he was alive. Trinh Khue immediately asked what position he was currently holding, Luc Dung Thanh replied: "Working as Quan Chanh4 in the underworld." Then he took out two books and gave them to Trinh Khue. The first book is Hieu Nghia Tu, the second book is Releasing Life Luc.

NOTE 2

Belongs to Zhejiang province.

NOTE 3

The original work uses “filial piety” (孝廉), which is another term for someone who has passed a bachelor's degree. This calling was used in the Ming and Qing dynasties.

NOTE 4

Quan Chanh (觀政): This official position does not exist in the earthly world, but according to the meaning, this person probably has the job of investigating and correcting everything properly.

Trinh Khue asked: "This book Release of Life was written by Great Master Lien Tri5, how can you get it in the underworld?" Luc Dung Thanh replied: "Every time Lord Yama comes across beautiful words and good deeds in the world, he orders them to be recorded and then circulated. If you follow that, you're just afraid that people won't believe it. If you can obey and follow it, your illness will be cured."

NOTE 5

Great Master Lien Tri (1532-1612) was from Hangzhou, surnamed Tham, alias Phat Tue, alias Lien Tri. The great master wrote about more than 30 works, such as Thien Quan Sach Tan, Pham Vong Gioi So Phat An, Amitabha Sutra So Sao, Hoa Nghiem Sutra of Touch...

Trinh Khue woke up from his dream and immediately went to find those two books and read them carefully. From then on, persevere in keeping the precept of not killing living things, and you will indeed be cured.

COMMENT

Ethics in life, there are only two paths, one is benevolent, the other is inhumane. Keeping the precept of not killing living things is kindness. Writing a book advising people to keep the precepts not to kill is to spread the virtue of kindness to others. Just by keeping the precept of doing good, that virtue is still small, but with many other people keeping the precept of doing good, that virtue is great.

Great Master Lien Tri is an outstanding servant of Confucianism, but views academics and reputation as a torn shoe. He left the worldly world and became a monk, becoming one who maintained the Buddhist precepts. Therefore, when he prayed for rain, it quickly rained. When he entered the mountains and forests, evil tigers hid and stayed away. So you know that, a book Living Life Luc teaching to keep the precepts not to kill, not even heaven and earth can do otherwise, let alone humans, let alone ghosts and gods?

Obstructing good deeds is punishable by death1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book of Evidence (證慈編). (Author's note.)

Trinh Tu Xuong was from Mat Chau.2 saw that the people in Giao Tay town loved to eat meat and kill many animals, so one night he lit incense and prayed to Bac Dau Tinh Quan: "Trinh Tu Xuong, I would like to dedicate myself for the sake of all sentient beings as well as my parents in the past seven generations to engrave a copy of the book 'Giat Tu Xuong' [to warn people to stop killing]. Today it is urgent.

NOTE 2

Belongs to Shandong province.

May the Lord of Heaven descend, help me rely on his divine power to carry out the circulation of this book smoothly.”

In the neighborhood there was a woman named Hoa, the wife of Mr. Peng Canh. When she received the book, she immediately tore it up and threw it into a dirty place. The next day, Mrs. Hoa bought a fish and was about to slaughter it. The fish suddenly jumped up and blinded her. The blood flowed out and turned into poisonous worms, crawling all over her body.

That story spread everywhere, the Provincial Governor Quach Huong suddenly saw a god appear and said: "I am Bac Dau Tinh Quan. I have observed that in this area there is a person with a good heart, Trinh Tu Xuong, who spent money to engrave and print the book 'Precepts of killing and teaching' to publish it. Mrs. Hoa threw that book into a dirty place, the crime is very serious, she must die. For those who [have read the book and] refuse to accept it. If you repent, you will have to pay for your sins. When I come down here next time, I will punish you all.”

COMMENT

People born in a time of moral decline, evil karma are increasing day by day, good roots are becoming less and less, so when they see others doing a good deed, saying a good word, how many people do not stop or disturb them? For example, when we see others keeping the precepts of not killing, we will say that "That's doing something in vain in vain", that "That person is not blessed [to enjoy delicious food]"... Or when we see others doing things to release animals, we will say that "If we let them go, we won't be sure of them

to live", that "If you are released, you will soon be captured by someone else"... Some people even laugh and criticize and slander, saying that there is no cause and effect. Or in the middle of a crowded place, they criticize the unclear doubts of the person who does good deeds; or point out and dig up the mistakes and shortcomings of that person, calling them foolish. [Deeds like that] makes people who have just developed the intention to do good deeds unable to help but feel confused in their hearts, turn back their weak good minds and stop doing good deeds.

Oh, people with such evil minds, the gods see them all angry, seeing them as evil demons, 1 how they will fall after death is already obvious, there is no need to say.

NOTE 1

The name of this demon is transcribed from the Sanskrit word Kumbhāṇḍa, which is a demon that specializes in eating human essence. Such a comparison is to say that preventing others from doing good deeds is no different from a demon sucking on a person's essence, because it causes that person's good roots to be weakened and destroyed.

Therefore, I would like to advise those who have a good heart, whenever they meet someone who hinders good deeds, if they have all the slanderous words, please listen quietly, do not pay attention to anger; [If you meet someone who can advise you, be sincere] advise you, don't use arrogant and contemptuous words; [For those who can't be persuaded,] you should feel pity for the poor, don't have a heart of hatred and alienation. Looking at the [retribution] story of Mrs. Hoa, isn't it very scary?

tieu_de: Advice to officials
noi_dung:
Advice to officials1

NOTE 1

The following stories advise officials not to kill living things. (Author's note) Originally, the engraving "Early mandarin" (宰官) was engraved to specifically refer to the leading mandarins in the industry or locality. This implies that if the top mandarin knows how to limit killing, he will have an influence on his subordinates. But considering the content of the article, there really is advice that is suitable for officials.

All over the world, in terms of luxury or poverty, no one is the same. There are people who leisurely ride in four-horse carriages with utmost dignity. There are also people who always have to carry heavy loads on their backs, drifting here and there in loneliness and misery. There are people who live rich and peaceful lives, with honor and glory, with treasures full of gold, silver, and jewels. There are certainly people who don't have enough to eat and have no choice but to sadly beg for food. The glories or humiliations in the human world, compared to each other, are as different as heaven and earth.

If you do not believe in the Buddhist theory of cause and effect or retribution for many lifetimes, you must see that what God gives to humans is extremely unfair. Therefore, in the Sutras it is taught: "To be a noble person, to be a wealthy king, is all due to the good cause of being respectful and serving the Three Jewels; to be a rich person is all due to the good cause of giving alms to help others; to be a long-lived person, is all due to the good cause of keeping the precepts [not killing]; to be a person with a dignified and beautiful appearance, is all due to the good cause of being patient. Whatever the previous life created, so will be the result in this life. Just like the person in charge of ritual music, when the bell rings, the bell will ring, and when the bell rings, the bell will ring. echo

opens up; or like a gardener, if you plant peaches, you will reap peaches, if you plant tangerines, you will reap tangerines.” That's the difference between being rich or poor.

Like a bell ringer, when he uses a big bell, he hears a loud sound, when he uses a small bell, he hears a small sound, until he is like a gardener, who plants one tree and gets to reap the fruit of one tree, and when he plants ten trees, he gets to reap the fruit of ten trees. There are different levels of being rich or poor because of that.

Today we see people at a young age who have passed high scores, enjoyed high official positions, and received many benefits, it is because that person in their previous life loved to do good deeds tirelessly and widely cultivated merit. If that is not the reason, then why does the blue sky only reserve goodness for those who are officials?

People who are in high positions, rely on their power and can call and dictate to others, so if they want to do good, they must be strong enough to do good, but if they do evil, they also have the power to do evil. This is similar to using ginseng and phoenix medicines, which can help people recover from illness, but if used without caution can also cause illness. That's why Mencius said: "Only people with good hearts should be in high positions."

Furthermore, the higher the hierarchical position, the more people kill animals for daily cooking, parties, and entertaining guests and friends. When arriving at a place, the animals on land and in the

water surrounding them all have to endure the tragedy of being chopped up and cut into pieces [to take care of their food and drink]. A day in the position of an official is a day when countless innocent animals have to endure torture one after another.

Therefore, virtuous high-ranking mandarins of the past often felt compassion for living beings without fear of cause and effect. Depending on where they went, they set up river sections for releasing animals, and often hung signs prohibiting slaughter. If an order is issued "those who kill buffaloes will be punished", the herd of buffaloes that are trembling in fear will be happy to survive the slaughter. If an order "banning the killing of dogs" is issued, so many guard dogs will escape the tragedy of being punished by their owners with knives and chopping boards.

Even through things like encircling mountains and forests and chasing away animals to hunt, draining rivers and lakes to catch fish,1 [good mandarins] strictly admonish, issue orders, and prohibit all conditions for killing living things.

NOTE 1

These are forms of mass killing in the past. When organizing a hunt, people surround each area of ​​the forest and mountains, beat drums and gongs loudly to drive away wild animals in one direction, and then have people waiting there to shoot and kill them all. For ponds and lakes, drain the water and catch them all, regardless of size.

The only fear is that one day when the power and position no longer exist, even if you have a good heart, you will not have the power to do good. Therefore, we strongly advise all those still in office to quickly sow good seeds and, using the existing good conditions, create blessings for all people. That is respectfully obeying the love for life of heaven and earth, in accordance with

the court's benevolence and generosity. Once you gain power, you immediately become more virtuous. If you can save the lives of all species, don't hesitate and delay. Those who hold high positions should advise their subordinates to strictly prohibit slaughter. Those with minor positions should petition their superiors to stop the killing of living things. If one can keep the virtue of benevolence passed down through the generations, one's name will be recorded in the book of heaven and earth, which means doing virtuous deeds in just one life and enjoying profound blessings for many more lives to come. But [when there is power in hand but] cannot do so, is it like a person who goes into a mountain of treasure but returns empty-handed and takes nothing?

Engrave a stone stele to pass down the virtue of kindness1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book "Old Tang History” (舊唐史). (Editor's note.)

During the Tang Dynasty, there was Mr. Nhan Chan Khanh, whose full name was Thanh Than,2 was very good at calligraphy. He respectfully served the Three Jewels and had received precepts from Zen master Tue Minh in Ho Chau.

NOTE 2

Nhan Chan Khanh was born in 709, died in 785, was from Lam Nghi, Shandong province, and was once given the title Duke of Lu, so he was also called Nhan Lu Cong. He is the 7th generation grandson of the Northern Qi Dynasty scholar Nhan Su Co, and the 5th generation grandson of Nhan Chi Thoi, author of the book Nhan Thi Gia Tu. He passed his doctorate in the reign of Khai Nguyen in the reign of Emperor Huyen Tong, served as a mandarin through four dynasties, reaching positions such as Thi Lang of the Ministry of Household, Minister of the Ministry of Justice, Chief of Royal History...

In the reign of Can Nguyen, the 3rd year,3 king

NOTE 3

That is the year 760.

Duong Tuc Tong established ponds to release animals in the country, calculated in all districts, important river wharfs or riverside areas, suburbs... a total of up to 81 places. In each such place, Nhan Chan Khanh asked the king to grant an epitaph and engrave it on the stone stele so that it could be passed on to future generations without being damaged. He held the position of Minister of the Right Vehicle, was given the title of Duke Lu, and was a famous mandarin for a time.

FOR DECLARATION

When setting up a pond to release animals, you should ask your superiors for a stone stele to be erected, [clearly stating] that all fishing boats are prohibited from approaching, so that it can have a long-lasting effect.

The stele that Nhan Lo Cong asked the king to grant, although said to be controlled by the emperor, were actually written by him. From the Tang Dynasty to the present1 for more than a thousand years, countless lives have been saved, and the virtue sown is boundless, all thanks to his enlightenment efforts.

NOTE 1

That is during the time of Mr. Chu An Sy.

Fish crying touching people2

NOTE 2

Excerpted from the book Quang Nhan Luc (廣仁錄). (Author's note)

During the Song Dynasty, Mr. Phan Hoa was a district official in Chu Ky, practiced the Samantabhadra dharma, and issued an order prohibiting fishing. When he obeyed the edict and was about to return to the capital, he suddenly dreamed that there were tens of thousands of fish in the river crying and saying to him: "Go away, chief.

from here, our fish family cannot avoid being killed and cooked.” After speaking, he cried even louder, the echo was so loud.

Mr. Phan Hoa was surprised, immediately wrote the text "Mong fish ky" (Recounting the dream of seeing fish), then instructed his successor to [continue to maintain the ban on catching fish].

COMMENT

The hearts of saints, could it be that they do not want to give to everyone? Can all species live in peace? The only thing is, the situation of species [raised solely for slaughter] such as goats, pigs, [chickens, ducks...] makes it difficult to prohibit people from killing them. As for animals such as buffaloes [raised to plow the fields,] dogs [raised to protect the house], or species [that live in the wild] in the water [not raised by humans], all can be prohibited from killing.

There should be preparations many days in advance, clearly stating the ban. [After that,] if someone violates and brings animals [that are prohibited from killing] to sell, anyone has the right to confiscate, and at the same time bring both the evidence and the seller to the government for trial. People throughout the locality are forbidden from buying those animals. If there is a violator, anyone on the street who sees it has the right to confiscate it [bring it to the government for trial]. The important thing is to have strict rewards and punishments that do not change from time to time. If it could be done seriously and regularly like that, people would not be able to capture and kill animals in just one day, even if they wanted to kill them in just one day. This is called a complete prohibition, stopping right at the source of killing.

Two resurrections1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Touch Thien Quang So (感應篇廣疏). (Author's note)

Ngo District2 had a Justice Officer3 who suddenly fell dead. After waking up one night, he quickly called his family and told them to invite the Prefect4 and all his fellow officials and subordinates to come, then bowed his head, bowed to everyone and said: "I was arrested and taken to the underworld, I begged for my life. At first they did not agree, but then asked me: 'Can you advise a thousand people not to eat buffalo meat? I will give you 3 days to do so.' Now I am lucky to be alive. again, but if you did not advise the people throughout the region for my sake, this would not be possible.”

NOTE 2

This is now the Phuyang region of Zhejiang province.

NOTE 3

Judiciary: an official leading the local judicial branch. method.

NOTE 4

Prefect: the top official of the entire district.

Everyone [didn't believe it was true, so] they just pretended to make empty promises [and then no one did anything]. After three days, the Justice Officer actually fell down and died. The Thai governor was extremely frightened, immediately summoned all the officials in the district, together vowed to keep the precept not to eat buffalo meat, and placed a book at the intersection, advising people to write their names there [to vow not to eat buffalo meat]. When the number of one thousand people was reached, the list was burned. Buffalo meat] will bring immeasurable blessings.”

NOTE 1

Each era is 12 years, plus 6 eras is 72 years.

That Justice later lived to be a hundred years old.

CONCLUSION

In recent times,2 local officials have also issued a ban on killing buffaloes, but lack of implementation methods. Therefore, even though signs prohibiting the killing of buffaloes were hung all over the city, buffalo meat dishes were everywhere.

NOTE 2

That was during the time of Mr. Chu An Si.

People who slaughtered buffaloes were only greedy for profit. If you don't give them benefits, they will naturally quit their job. We should send dispatchers to take turns controlling [everywhere]. If we catch someone selling buffalo meat, we will fine them and use that money to reward the person who caught them. The amount of that reward must be greater than the amount of private bribes received by buffalo slaughterers. In this way, the translator will happily follow the official orders without accepting bribes to cover up the violators. If we don't do that, once the service department has received bribes from the slaughterhouses and colluded to cover for them, how will local officials know? How can it be detected?

Forbidden to kill buffaloes to increase life expectancy1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Precepts of Ox Vocabulary (戒牛彙編). (Author's note)

During the Gia Tinh era, the2 governor of Fujian province, Hu Dat, held a banquet to welcome guests. At that time, the Minister Lam Tuan, who was attending a party, suddenly felt dizzy and fell into a coma. He kept shaking and did not wake up. After a very long time, he suddenly regained consciousness and said: "It's strange! I was indeed taken to the underworld. The judge was the ancestor of my family, the Minister Lam Thong the day before. He told me: 'The current King of Diem La is Pham Van Chanh,3 I am his subordinate. In the past, I was a district official who did not prohibit the killing of buffaloes, and my life expectancy was reduced by a century,4 That's why I brought you here today.' I immediately argued: 'When I accepted the position of district commander, there was indeed an order prohibiting the killing of buffaloes, the document is still there today.' He was surprised and said: 'Is there a mistake?' Immediately ordered a re-examination. In a moment, the district governor brought my sign prohibiting the killing of buffaloes.

NOTE 2

The Gia Tinh era was in the Minh The dynasty. Tong, from 1522 to 1566.

NOTE 3

Pham Van Chanh, also known as Pham Trong Yem (范仲淹), was born in 989, died in 1052, his given name was Hy Van, his posthumous name was Van Chanh.

NOTE 4

A century: 12 years.

issued the day before the submission. He was very happy, presented it on my behalf, and immediately had my life expectancy returned to me for a century. He sent someone to take me home."

The guests at the party that day were all frightened, and together they swore not to eat buffalo meat again. Lam Tuan later lived for exactly another century.

DECLARATION

The desire of the poor is to be rich, the hope is to be rich. The wish of the rich is to be noble, the only wish of the noble is to live long. In the dark and gloomy world, just by killing buffaloes, among those who are officials, there are many people who [forbid killing buffaloes] have their lifespan increased, how many people [because they are not banned from killing buffaloes] have their lifespans reduced? It's just a pity that the world of hell and world are separate, so people cannot clearly know that.

tieu_de: Advice to those who work at customs
noi_dung:
Advice to those working at the mandarin gate

Those who work at the gate often see others being tied up in shackles, or being beaten and interrogated, with almost no mercy. Therefore, they consider keeping the precept of not killing to be even more unrealistic and unrealistic. Therefore, once they go to a village, they are unruly and unrestrained. When they see chickens, they take chickens, when they see ducks, they take ducks.

even force people to sell their children1 to have money to feed themselves. Being satisfied like that and then flaunting these things in their own ranks, claiming to be talented, makes such brutality develop more and more. They don't know that heaven's way of repaying debt is not wrong, [the violent people] cannot help but die by sword and stick, or perish in prison, or their family business will be ruined, and their children and grandchildren will have to be poor and beg for food everywhere. All such retributions are caused by a cruel and cruel mind, causing them to suffer evil retributions in this life.

NOTE 1

The law at that time allowed people to sell themselves as slaves to others in exchange for some money. Parents also have the right to sell their children, and husbands have the right to sell their wives. Therefore, when poor people are forced to pay certain amounts of money to local officials and cannot manage it, they must sell their children to pay, otherwise they will be imprisoned or beaten.

Therefore, I would like to widely advise all good-hearted people working in official positions to regularly create means to help people. Seeing a miserable person having to go to the mandarin's gate, he should use kind words to comfort him. When she met a relative who was lonely, she suffered unjustly, so for that person she went to the public square to confess her injustice. When it comes to eating and drinking, it's truly limitless, there are so many dishes that can satisfy our appetites and fill our hearts. If [killing life-giving creatures makes] the heavens angry, how can [simple vegetable soup] enjoy blessings, increase longevity, and help future descendants enjoy prosperity?

The ancients said: "The same arm can push people down, can support people; the same morsel of food, can kill, can save lives." People who clearly understand that principle, perhaps do not consider it carefully?

Accomplice with bad people is punished by the underworld1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Guan Kin Luc (觀感錄). (Author's note)

In the year of Giap Than in the reign of Sung Trinh,2 Thieu Thu Phuong worked in Long Du district.3 At that time, the district official banned slaughter, the butchers in the village were afraid that the patrolling service would find them and not leave it alone, so they bribed Thu Phuong with money to prevent and cover up. Thanks to that, they can still freely slaughter.

NOTE 2

That is the year 1644. The Sung Trinh era lasted from 1628 to 1644, under the reign of Minh Tu Tong.

NOTE 3

Long Du District belongs to Zhejiang Province.

In the year of At Dau,4 on April 2, Thu Phuong died, and after 7 days suddenly came back to life, saying that she had gone to the underworld and saw the Judge investigating the matter of killing the buffalo. Suddenly, a buffalo ran to bite him, and saw that the butcher named Vuong Thap Nhat was also there, wanting to blame Thu Phuong. At that time, a buffalo butcher knife and a basin of blood suddenly appeared right in front of her, and Thu Phuong immediately tried her best to complain. The judge said: "Even if you didn't kill the buffalo yourself, if it weren't for your cover that day, the butchers would have been afraid of being caught by the district judge, and would not have dared to kill the buffalo." The Tradition examined again and found that Thu Phuong's lifespan had not yet ended, so he sent her back to the living world, waiting for her crime to be punished after death.

NOTE 4

That is, the year 1645.

COMMENT

As for the ban on animal slaughter, if you let it go, it would be very easy, but if you strictly prohibit it, it would be very difficult. Therefore, once you have influenced others to let go of the prohibition, it is considered that you yourself have received the retribution of wearing feathers and horns.1 Therefore, those who are in public positions must be very careful!

NOTE 1

Wearing feathers and horns: it means having to be reborn in animals.

tieu_de: Advise people to take care of their parents
noi_dung:
Advising people to take care of their parents2

NOTE 2

The following stories advise people not to kill at home.

Children practice filial piety and care. Parents also have many different ways, [which can be divided into hierarchies].

Being able to wholeheartedly take care of your parents according to your subordinates is called minor filial piety. Being able to wholeheartedly take care of your parents according to hierarchy is called filial piety. Being able to wholeheartedly take care of your parents according to your superiors is called great filial piety. Only those who can wholeheartedly take care of their parents according to the highest level can be called great filial people in the great filial piety.

What does that mean? Taking care of your parents according to your subordinates means only taking care of your parents with enough food, clothing, delicious food, and not letting your parents have anything to complain about. That is also something that worldly people cannot easily do, called little filial piety.

Caring for parents according to hierarchy, that is to say [in addition to providing adequate food and clothing] also paying attention to the parents' aspirations. What my parents love, I also love, what my parents respect, I also respect, making my parents always happy. This is called filial piety.

Serving your parents according to the superiors means [in addition to the above things, also] leading and encouraging your parents to walk on the path. When you see your parents doing good, you approve, if you see your parents doing something wrong, you dissuade them, so that your words and actions are in accordance with the Right Path. That's called great filial piety.

As for taking care of your parents in the ultimate way, that is [after doing the above and] going one step further, always thinking of your parents' gratitude, which is as great as heaven and earth, but your parents' lifespan is decreasing day by day. What method should you use to repay them? What methods can be used to prolong the life of parents? What methods can be used to help parents escape the cycle of birth and death? What methods can be used to help parents eliminate all sins and karma? What method can be used to help parents [increase their practice, gain enlightenment and attain enlightenment] to join the holy lineage and eventually become Buddha?

is that okay? If you escape to the open sea, will the robbers come? Hiding in the vast wilderness, will the bandits come? If you think carefully like that, you will definitely be able to bring your parents to a place of peace in all aspects. To be able to do so is called taking care of one's parents in a supreme way, in a way that can't be better than anything else. It's also called taking care of one's parents in a way that transcends all worldly dharmas. Isn't that a person of great filial piety?

[If you often reflect on the above, you will see that,] if you kill animals to raise your parents, it will cause the killed animals to hold resentment for many lives, and the parents will have to be reincarnated many lives to repay the debt of killing. That's better than using poisoned meat to offer your parents to relieve hunger, or using poisoned wine to hope your parents will quench their thirst. It's extremely unreasonable, how can you wrongly call that filial piety?

Someone asked: "Can a scholar who achieves success, glorifies his family, honors his ancestors, be considered filial?" Answered: "Achieving fame and fortune is of course something we should pursue. If we know how to rely on it to do good and help others, it will definitely make our parents happy and honored, but if we rely on it to do bad things, wouldn't it be humiliating our parents? The parents of Tan Coi,1 Nghiem Tung all have children

NOTE 1

Qin Hui (1090-1155): a notorious traitor in Chinese history, manipulated the court during the reign of Song Cao Tong (1107 - 1187), falsely accused and murdered countless loyal and loyal officials, including the famous general Nhac Phi. People in later generations hated him so much that when they built a temple to worship Nhac Phi (Muc Mieu) in Hang Chau, they had statues of the couple Qin Hui - Vuong Thi cast in handcuffs. Kneel down in front of the temple and let people pass by and spit on the two. To this day, the Chinese rice cake and porridge dish made with dough fried in oil still maintains the custom of making each pair stick together and is considered a symbol of Tan Coi and his wife being tied up in pairs and thrown into an oil cauldron for punishment.

boys are mandarins in the rank of Prime Minister at the top of the court,1 but if they were born in this life, they would inevitably be hated and hated by people."

NOTE 1

Nghiem Tung: a traitor during the reign of Emperor Gia Tinh (ie Minh The Tong, 1507 - 1567). Nghiem Tung was He was illiterate and had no talent, but he was so good at flattery that Emperor Gia Tinh assigned him to take charge of all political affairs from 1539. From then on, he manipulated all court affairs and harmed innocent loyal people. By April 1562, Emperor Gia Tinh saw Nghiem Tung's incompetence and cunning, immediately listened to his loyal officials and ordered the entire Nghiem family to be punished The number of officials in this case is more than 50,000 people.

Therefore, we must know that if a filial child wants to honor his parents, there is nothing better than doing good and accumulating merit. Achieving good reputation should only be considered a secondary thing.

Repaying for bad karma2

NOTE 2

Excerpted from the book Hieu Sinh Luc (好生錄). (Author's note)

Jiaxing County [Zhejiang Province] has an old woman who lives thanks to her son who is a crabber. Every day he caught crabs, tied them with grass strings and sold them, using the money to buy rice, firewood... everything to take care of his mother.

One ​​day, the old woman was sick and suddenly took the long grass strings and gradually swallowed them into her stomach. Swallow it all in, then grab each strand, pulling each strand back out. Pulling it all out, swallowing it back

in, then pulling it back out again, doing so over and over again, causing blood to flow out of the mouth from the intestines. The old woman said again: "I was raised by the money created by my son's bad karma, so now I have to suffer this kind of retribution. If it weren't like this, I'm afraid I would have suffered even more."

There were many people who came to watch, and after many days like this, the old woman died.

EXCUSSION

Once upon a time, when the World-Honored One was in Rajagaha, he saw a large fish with many heads, each head different, caught in a net. Seeing this, the World-Honored One immediately entered Samadhi, raised his mind of compassion, and called out to the fish. Fish immediately responded. The Buddha asked him: "Where is your mother now?" The fish replied: "Your mother is now a worm in the toilet." The Buddha immediately taught the Bhikkhus: "That big fish at the time of the Buddha Kasyapa1 was a Bhikkhu who was well-versed in the Tripitaka. Due to creating bad karma, he suffered a deformed karma, a body with many heads. The Bhikkhu's mother received his care, and because of that karma, now he has to be a worm in the toilet."

NOTE 1

Buddha Kasyapa is the Buddha born right before Buddha Shakyamuni, one of the 7 Buddhas of this lifetime.

Contemplating this, one must see that using money created by bad karma to support parents is not something a filial child should do,

not to mention are accustomed to following the custom of killing things to offer to their parents?

Remains of previous karma1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Guan Kin Luc (觀感錄). (Author's note)

During the Qing Dynasty, there was Mr. Co Thuan Chi, a native of Thuong Thuc district,2 was a vegetarian, residing in Wuxi district.3 On the first day of the second month of the year Canh Tuat under the reign of Khang Hy,4 he closed his eyes and fell asleep for seven days before waking up and telling people around him:

NOTE 2

Belongs to Suzhou, Jiangsu province.

NOTE 3

Also belongs to Jiangsu province.

NOTE 4

That is, in 1670, The 9th year of the Kangxi era.

"I dreamed that a religious person came to invite me to listen to the sutras. I went with him to a certain place and saw that the front dharma hall was preaching the Diamond Sutra, and the back dharma hall was preaching the Retribution Sutra. At the end of the lecture, I heard the teaching: 'Vegetarian people must persevere in keeping the Buddha's name in mind; meat eaters must essentially keep the precepts of not killing. By doing so, one can pray for the salvation of their parents for many generations, and two can eliminate sins. my own karmic fault.' "Then a moment later, I suddenly saw my mother crying in a lake filled with blood, with snails and earthworms surrounding her entire body. The wise man told me: 'Your mother in this life has already been transcended. You see that she is the mother in your previous life. Because when she was alive, she liked to eat ducks, so now she has to be surrounded by those animals. You should recite the Rebirth Mantra to pray for her to pass away.’ Then he woke up.”

DECLARATION

People call it filial piety, but it's only [worrying about parents] in the present life. People who follow the Buddha's teachings with great filial piety benefit their parents for many lifetimes, so it is called great filial piety.

tieu_de: Advice to those who love their children
noi_dung:
Advice to those who love their children

Children kill animals because their parents do not stop them. Once they get used to killing, they see it as just a normal thing. At first, if you don't have compassion for small insects like ants, crickets, etc., then you will do things like slaughtering buffaloes and killing dogs without seeing any need to stop them. Once compassion is lost, good reputation disappears, descendants will be cut off, everything depends on that. So know that from childhood, if you train yourself to do good deeds, you will definitely become a good person. If you practice evil deeds, you will definitely become an evil person. You cannot relax even for a day without paying attention to teaching.

Please give me a generous advice to all parents: even if they are small, they should be saved, and children in the house, even when they are still young, must be careful to teach and prevent them. How to make sure that everything your children see and hear is all good and kind. Even a person who has become inhumane should still be taught and enlightened, not to mention [children who all have] a kind nature? If not

so, when you were young, you didn't worry about teaching, and later on you would have no time to regret it.

The Tang family told stories of the underworld1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Guan Kin Luc (觀感錄). (Author's note)

Thang Sinh is from Lat Thuy district,2 in the year Giap Ngo in the year Thuan Tri3 attended the Huong exam, but just after finishing the exam he fell ill. By around midnight on October 6 of that year, his whole body was cold and stiff, and all the things he had done in his life suddenly appeared clearly before his eyes. He remembered that when he was young, he playfully caught a chicken and hid it in the gutter, but a ground squirrel bit it and injured it. One time he killed an entire nest of bats. Another time, there was a maid in the house who fell asleep, and he used burning oil paper and burned his hand.

NOTE 2

Belongs to Jiangsu province.

NOTE 3

That is the year 1654, the year of Thuan Tri. 11.

Then in a split second, he suddenly saw a flock of bats coming to demand his life, and he was extremely scared. But then he suddenly remembered all the good deeds he had done, no matter how small they were. Suddenly he remembered a sentence in the Heart Sutra "without obstacles trying, without terror" (the mind has no obstacles so there is no fear or panic). Once he understood a little, his heart gradually felt at peace. Suddenly he saw the Venerable Avalokiteśvara appearing high above, holding a poplar branch and splashing water, and immediately woke up. Later, in the year of Tan Suu,4 he passed his doctorate.

NOTE 4

That is the year 1661.

COMMENT

The Thang family caged chickens and killed bats, all of which were playful things in their childhood. But when they reach the underworld, the animals that were killed immediately appear and demand their lives, so it can be clearly known that the crime of killing animals is not tolerated even by children. What's more, when children play and cause harm, it's not just with a chicken or a bat? Those who truly love their children must urgently consider this danger and take early steps to prevent it.

Destroying the bird's nest and burning the feet dry1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Hieu Sinh Luc (好生錄). (Author's note)

In Ky Chau district2 there is a child who often searches for bird nests and then catches eggs to eat. One day, someone told it: "There are bird eggs over there, you can come with me to catch them." The child immediately followed that person to a mulberry field. Suddenly he saw that on the left side of the road there was a city, inside the city there were houses, very beautiful and crowded roads, and there was bustling music and noise. The child was surprised and asked: "When did this city exist?" The person accompanying him shouted at him not to speak, then led him into the city. As soon as he entered, the city gate suddenly closed, the city was full of red-hot iron under his feet, the heat was unbearable. The child screamed and ran quickly to the south city gate. As soon as he arrived, the city gate immediately closed.

NOTE 2

Belongs to Hebei province.

Running to the east gate, then west, north, every time you arrive, you will see the city gate naturally closed tightly.

At that time, in the mulberry field, there was a person picking mulberry leaves. Seeing the child running and screaming in the mulberry field, he thought he was crazy and ran back to tell his father. The father arrived and called out the child's name. As soon as the child responded, he immediately fell to the ground, and the whole citadel and its hot fire were no longer visible. The father looked at his son's legs and saw that from the knees down they were charred as if they were being grilled on fire. When asked, he immediately recounted what had happened. The father took him home to take care of the treatment, and in the end the baby's legs from the knees down were just like two dry bones.

COMMENT

Suffering in hell is created by the mind, and also manifests in the mind. For people with profound merit, hell is also the palace of heaven. Those who commit heavy evil karma will immediately turn the heavenly palace into hell. Just like a person with malaria is in the same place as a person without the disease, but the person without the disease does not feel cold, while the other person with the disease shivers like he is in the middle of an icy place. There are times when people who are not sick don't feel hot, but the sick person sweats like a bath, as if they are in a hot fire. That's one thing to prove.

Like the gods in the Six Desires heavens, 1 although they enjoy the same heavenly food, those with more merit and virtue see that food as completely white and clean, while those with less merit and virtue, depending on the degree, see that dish as more or less darker in color. Even things like clothes, jewels, palaces... are all different in the same way. That's another reason to prove it.

NOTE 1

The Six Desire Heavens: refers to the 6 heavens of the Desire Realm, including: 1. The Four Great Kings of Heaven; 2. Thirty-three heavens; 3. Da-ma heaven; 4. Tushita Heaven; 5. Happiness transforms heaven; 6. Self-transformation in heaven.

Just like when people are in their mother's womb, everything is surrounded by the five internal organs, blood and blood, but when the World-Honored One is in the womb of the holy mother Maya, entering the Samadhi of Lycracy, all kinds of fragrant wood, sandalwood, wonderful jewels, countless palaces appear to adorn themselves. Isn't that all created by the mind?

Therefore, we know that when a child hears someone say "there is an egg over there", it is created from within his own mind, an egg of ignorance. In the mulberry field, there is a citadel, which also appears from its own mind, a citadel of unjust karma created. All over the city there is hot fire, also appearing from the heart, it is the hot fire of affliction. The four gates of the city are all closed by themselves, and it is also from their own mind that the prison gates appear. That's why there is a saying: "Hell is not far, it is right before your eyes, depending on each person's karma, it will appear."

tieu_de: Women should be advised
noi_dung:
Women should be advised

The Kinh Thi has a saying: “As a woman, there is no need to care about right or wrong, good or bad in the family, just focusing on cooking is good.”1 As for cooking, if you regularly slaughter and cut, you will gradually become better. become a habit that is very difficult to change. If one is not a person who has planted good roots many lives ago, it will be very difficult to believe and accept and keep the precept of not killing.

NOTE 1

The original is: “女子無非無儀 ，唯酒食是議“ (The woman has no concubine, no doubt, only wine eats thi de), taken from the Kinh Poetry, section Tieu Nha, Thien Tu Can, chapter 9. The original text of this poem is: “乃生女子, 載 寢之地，載衣之裼，載弄之瓦, 無非無儀，唯酒食是議, 無父母詒罹。” re-soaked the ground, re-clothed the body, re-dressed the road, without doubt, only wine and practice, no mother and divorce.) Roughly translated: "If a girl is born, let her sleep on the ground, put a diaper on, take a tile for her to play with. Growing up, there's no need to discuss right and wrong, good or bad, just worry about food and drink for the family, and don't bring worries to your parents."

But the woman in the family takes care of the kitchen, so she is almost the one who has the power to decide whether or not to kill animals. If you are a person with the virtue of loving life and wanting to protect life, why don't you use benevolent principles to teach and inspire the women in your family?

Thanks to copying sutras, one can escape suffering2

NOTE 2

Excerpted from the book Dharma euphemism Chau Lam (法苑珠林). (Author's note) However, we did not find this story in the Phap Uyen Chau Lam but found it in volume 1 of the book Vajra Sutra Sutra Sutra Sutra Touching Luc (金剛經受持感應錄), classified in the Van Tuc Pitaka, sutra number 1631, page 474, sheet c, starting from the 5th line. This book again cites the source from Ming Pao Ky (冥報記). We have compared the content in the Ming Pao Ky book and found that there are some details that are different from the content in the Complete Book of An Si.

During the Tang Dynasty, around the first year of Long Shuo's reign,1 in Lac Chau district2 there was a person named Ngu Ngu Nuong. After dying for more than a month, he dreamed 3 to his sister and younger brother: "When I was young, I had scabies. I killed a crab and crushed it to apply it. Although the scabies were cured at that time, but now I have to Falling into hell, there are 7 blades piercing my body, the pain is unbearable. Please do Buddhist work to dedicate the merit to save me."4

NOTE 1

That is in the year 661, Emperor Cao Tong's reign.

NOTE 1

NOTE 2

This is now Lac Duong, in Ha Nam province.

NOTE 3

According to Minh Bao Ky, it was not a dream, but in the middle of the night both the older sister and the younger brother heard a groan on the altar, immediately asked and heard the voice of the dead man answering.

NOTE 4

According to Minh Bao Ky, this paragraph also has some other details, perhaps Mr. An Si omitted them. In addition, this book records Ngu Ngu Nuong saying: "Please accept my clothes and help me do meritorious deeds." After that, the sister saw the clothes that had been shrouded with her when she was buried and were now lying on the bed. Thus, there is no detail of bringing the dead person's clothes to the pagoda (This is not reasonable).

The sister immediately brought the clothes left by Ngu Ngu Nuong to the Pure Land Pagoda to make offerings, and asked Master Bao Hien to copy 7 volumes of the Diamond Sutra. Just after copying the sutra, I dreamed that Ngu Ngu Nuong appeared in my dream5 to thank her and say: "Now all 7 knife tips have come out of my body. Thanks to that blessing, I have been reborn."

NOTE 5

According to Minh Bao Ky, it was still not a dream, but I heard a voice from the altar.

CONCLUSION

Killing an animal's life to cure an illness is impossible, let alone creating the karma of killing for no reason!

Flies and ants want their lives together1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Quan Quan Luc (觀感錄). (Author's note)

At the end of the Ming Dynasty, Wuxi County2 lived a man named Du who, from the age of more than twenty, began to be a vegetarian and worship Buddha. It's just that he really hates flies and ants, and kills them as soon as he sees them.

NOTE 2

Belongs to Jiangsu province.

At the age of seventy-two, he was very sick. He suddenly shouted loudly to the people around him that there were countless ants crawling into his mouth, and said that there were thousands of flies coming to claim his life. Moments later, seeing a medium leading the soul to him, he immediately died.

FOR DECLARATION

Considering the fact that the Du family likes to kill flies and ants along with the bad karma at the time of death, it is certain that his vegetarianism and Buddha worship were just a mere formality. If that were not the case, then the Tathagata would have immeasurable power. Just reciting the Buddha's name single-mindedly could exempt him from serious sins for many lifetimes. Not to mention, if he practiced all his life, why wouldn't he be exempt from sins in the present? Moreover, if you sincerely worship Buddha, how can you still [heartlessly] want to kill flies and ants?

tieu_de: Advise people not to keep cats
noi_dung:
Advising people not to keep cats

People create negative karma, just like growing vines. From a root that has grown, the branches and leaves will spread out. Consider raising a cat, for example. If viewed from a worldly perspective, this only creates bad karma [of killing rats]. But if you use clear wisdom and look carefully, you will see that this can foster countless negative karma. Now try to present here just a few of them.

- In general, rats do not harm

people, but now we suddenly have a malicious desire to kill them, which is called killing without cause.

- We cannot kill ourselves, but we use raising

cats to kill mice, which is called instructing others to kill.

- Every time you see a cat catching a mouse, you immediately start the mind of joy

rejoicing, that is called seeing the killing and supporting the joy (depending on killing).

- Seeing a cat catch a lot of mice, then praising it, that

is called praising, praising the killing (praising the killing).

- Intentionally letting cats into places with many rats

[so that they can catch and kill them], that is called creating favorable conditions for killing (means of killing).

- In the heart of wishing for the cat to catch mice every day, that is called cultivating the wish to kill (vow to kill).

- In my heart, I wanted to raise a cat to kill mice

in my house, the result was that the cat actually killed my house mice, that is called intentional and precise killing (right killing), also called killing in connection with the killing mind of others (through mind killing).

- In the heart of wanting to raise a cat to kill mice

in one's own house, the cat also ends up killing mice in other people's houses, which is called stealing (the way of killing), also called killing that is not compatible with the killing mind of others (the way of killing).

- Raising a cat just because you want it to catch mice, but then

catch fish, buy fish for it to eat, that is called additional killing (increased killing).

- Making the people around us imitate

follow, our children and grandchildren imitate and do the same, killing lives, that is called killing that continues to spread without end (endless killing)...

Countless such evil karma, all arising from just one basic initial idea of wanting to raise a cat, can there be no end to it? strict force to prevent [that idea]?

Mouse Tha Van Poetry1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Ancient History Talks (古史談苑). (Author's note)

Ly Chieu Ho participated in the Hoi exam. The examiner looked over his article and thought that the writing was not good,

immediately removed and placed on top of the bookshelf. [When it was time to go to sleep,] a big mouse picked up that essay and dragged it to his pillow. The examiner immediately took it and put it back on the bookshelf, and the mouse moved it to the pillow. Three times in a row, the examiner was shocked, immediately reviewed and passed the essay.

After posting the board, the examiner immediately asked Ly Chieu Ho. He said, “[Maybe because] for three generations my family has never raised a cat [to kill mice].”

COMMENT

Raising an animal in the house is to create an additional portion of bad karma. The Bodhisattva Precepts Sutra1 teaches that: "Buddhists who raise animals such as cats, dogs, pigs... are committing the sin of contempt."2 The Upasaka Precepts Sutra teaches that: "Raising cats is a sin. Raising animals such as goats, pigs, etc. is a sin. Raising silkworms [spinning silk] is a sin."3

NOTE 1

That is, the Pham Vong Sutra (梵網經), 2 volumes, is classified in the Mahayana Canon of Volume 24, sutra number 1484. The quoted content is in volume 2, page 1007, sheet b, line 13.

NOTE 2

Misdemeanors: crimes that are less serious than serious crimes or paralyzing crimes. Although it is called lighter, it still pollutes the pure conduct of the practitioner.

NOTE 3

Actually, this passage is taken from the book Brahmanical Bodhisattva Precepts Sutra of the First Hidden Meanings (梵網菩薩戒經義疏發隱), 5 volumes, classified in the Vajrayana Pitaka. Volume 38, sutra number 679. This excerpt belongs to volume 5, page 201, sheet a, lines 14 and 15, but this book cites the source with the sentence "Upasaka precepts and clouds". We have not yet found the original text in this sutra.

The scriptures clearly teach this in many places, it's just a pity that people don't have enough opportunity to read it. People who know how to cherish the lives of all living things do not want to do things like growing flowers, raising fish... because they all lead to the killing of more and more animals.

I hope readers can consider these things carefully and not consider them meaningless words.

tieu_de: Advise people to wish happy birthday
noi_dung:
Advising people to wish happy birthday1

NOTE 1

The following advice is not to kill animals on occasions of celebration.

It is indeed a good thing to wish a happy birthday. happy, but we should think that today there are many children and grandchildren happily raising their cups to celebrate longevity. In the past, it was also on this day that our parents were born and had to endure many hardships!2

NOTE 2

This sentence is inspired by a verse in the Book of Poetry: “哀哀父母，生我劬 勞 - Whoever is the father and mother, gives birth to the island.” (I feel sorry for my parents, who gave birth to me through so many hardships." This poem speaks about the gratitude of our parents for giving birth and nurturing us.

People today, on the day of celebrating their life, only know how to kill their living creatures, hold parties to entertain relatives and friends, but hardly remember their parents' immense gratitude for nurturing them, that's really strange!

Alas, once a child is born, the parents have to waste so much mental energy, causing the parents to endure countless more sufferings and sorrows, until the day we reach old age, we create the karma of killing living creatures, implicating our parents, how can we have peace in our hearts?

Once upon a time, King Thai Tong, when he was on the noble throne, did not even dare to be happy on his birthday, let alone be happy. What about other people?

Dare to advise filial children, every time their birthday comes, they should sadly think: "Today there is really nothing for me to be carefree and happy! Because it was on this day in the past, to give birth to the unlucky child1 that is me, my parents had to face many dangers, facing life and death. Today there is really nothing for me to be carefree and happy! It is on this day In the past, my mother had to begin a long series of hard days, carrying and protecting me day and night, lying on the wet side and dry on the roller, spending many years without a peaceful sleep, [so what is fun?]

NOTE 1

Not funny: a humble statement admitting that one does not follow and continue the good things of one's parents.

Today there is really nothing for us to be carefree and happy about! Because now I have a complete wife and children, and safely enjoy the inheritance and inheritance [left by my parents], but I don't know where my [deceased] parents were born, how happy or miserable they were, [so what is happiness?]

If today I widely do good deeds, dedicating merit to my parents in the afterlife, I'm afraid I won't be able to make it in time, [let alone] how can I have the heart to remember my parents' hardships and hardships on this day? Gather together to kill living things, eat, drink, and sing busily? class="book-paragraph">Con Son district1 has a Thai lady named Hua, the mother of academic official Tu Tich Du. She is a vegetarian every day, likes to do good deeds, and recites Buddhist sutras without being lazy.

NOTE 1

Belongs to Jiangsu province. This is the hometown of Mr. Chu An Si.

The winter of the year Dinh Suu in the reign of Sung Trinh2 is the occasion to celebrate the 60th birthday of Lady Thai. On her birthday, Lady Thai only did good deeds, made offerings to monks, and used all the longevity offerings of her friends to use in printing the Lotus Sutra. For all those who came to wish them longevity, Lady Thai arranged a vegetarian feast and brought out a set of printed sutras to give to each person.

NOTE 2

That is the year 1637, the 10th year of Sung Trinh, in the reign of Minh Tu Tong.

If knowledgeable people saw such a thing, who would everyone admires it. The Thai lady later lived a long and healthy life, and all her children and grandchildren prospered.

FOR DECLARATION

Other people on the day of celebration of life use wine and meat to entertain guests, [killing many life objects, so] on the contrary, they create evil causes that shorten their lifespan. The Tu family's mother knows how to use the taste of Dharma to respond to the hearts of those who wish her long life, that is, she has planted seeds to get the fruit of long life. Considering this, which side gains and which side loses, what should be abandoned

what should be followed, I hope that the reader can calm down in the quiet of the night and think carefully.

Using good deeds to treat guests1

NOTE 1

I witnessed this with my own eyes. (Author's note)

Con Son district has a man named Truong Bang Am, whose last name is Lap Liem,2 passed the exam in the year of the Rat in the year of Sung Trinh.3 He is a person who has practiced meritorious virtue for many generations, respectfully worships the Three Jewels, and is also dedicated to studying and learning the Dharma, often focusing on Zen Buddhism.

NOTE 2

Truong Lap Liem is the person who wrote the Preface to this book Van Thien Tien Tu.

NOTE 3

That is in 1636, the 9th year of Sung Trinh, in the reign of Minh Tu Tong.

In the fall of the year Ky Mui, it became the name Khang Hy4 was the occasion to celebrate his 60th birthday, people brought one after another bringing offerings to celebrate his longevity. Truong Bang Am brought all the gifts he received and used them to print the Pho Mon publication [in the Lotus Sutra] and the Great Compassion Mantra, which were in very large quantities. In entertaining and thanking those who came to congratulate, he also learned from the good deeds of Lady Hua Thai, being completely vegetarian and not killing any animals.

NOTE 4

That is in 1679, the 18th year of Kangxi's reign. According to this detail, Truong Bang Am was born in 1620, and thus he passed the exam in the year just 16 years old.

COMMENT

Friends and relatives bring gifts to celebrate life,

everyone thinks it's a good thing but doesn't know that it's unreasonable. If you are a person who cultivates good deeds and accumulates virtue, you will naturally enjoy a long life, so living a long life is just a matter of course, there is no need to show surprise and congratulate him? From the Tang and Ngu dynasties and before, people lived to be hundreds of years old without even mentioning congratulations. Later, people's merit became increasingly poor and their lifespan decreased, so longevity celebrations were held earlier and earlier. Alas! When the three calamities1 are about to happen, the short human lifespan is a sign that cannot be ignored. The work of Mr. [Truong Bang Am] can be said to be far beyond ordinary people.

NOTE 1

Three calamities (three disasters): fire disaster (fire disaster), water disaster (water disaster) and wind disaster (wind disaster). These three calamities will happen at the end of time, when the world is about to reach the stage of destruction.

Do not hold parties to celebrate, use money to help the poor2

NOTE 2

I witnessed this with my own eyes. (Editor's note)

Vien Ngo Quy, last name Tu, from Vu Lam,3 came to live in Con Son district. He often liked to do good deeds without getting tired.

NOTE 3

That is, Hangzhou.

In the early summer of the year of the Cat of the Kangxi era,4 he had just turned 50 years old. Friends who used to socialize with him invited each other to contribute money to organize a drinking party.

NOTE 4

That is, the year 1699, the 38th year of Kangxi's reign.

welcome, he tried to refuse but could not. He immediately invited everyone to Canh Duc Pagoda, received all the longevity contributions and distributed them to the poor, lonely and disabled people... He also spent his own money to contribute a part to the Charity Association and organized a [vegetarian party at the pagoda] to repay the kindness of all his friends.

DECLARATION

When ripe fruit waits for the day to fall; Once the tree has grown, it must wait for the day when it will be cut down for use. Therefore, a person with wisdom, from the time he reaches middle age, must always be alert, while living at home, he should visualize as if it were an inn. When dealing with relatives and relatives, he should visualize like friends. As each day passes, he should visualize himself as a fish lying in a shallow puddle, gradually drying up, [his life does not last long].1 If the time has come when his eyes become blurred, his teeth fall out, his hair turns gray and his back is thin, but he still indulges in the act of killing living beings. If you are ignorant and refuse to wake up, you are truly a foolish and incompetent person!2

NOTE 1

This passage is taken from the Dhammapada Sutra (法句經), 2 volumes, and is included in the Mahaskaya Canon of Volume 4, Sutra No. 210. This content is in volume 1, page 559, page a, line 26 - 27: 是日已過，　　命則隨減，　　如 少水魚，斯有何樂？- If the day is over, the life will be reduced, like the water and fish are few, private property is happy? (A day has passed, life has also decreased, like a fish lacking water, what joy is there?)

NOTE 2
