BOOK THREE

EXPLANATION OF DOUBTS

The mistake of the theory of “heaven created animals to feed people”1

NOTE 1

This section includes 6 question and answer sections. (Author's note)

Question: [The Book of Ministers, Thien Thai Oath says:]2 "Heaven and earth are the parents that give birth to all things. Of all things, humans are the most sacred, that's why heaven gives birth to animals, which are only to nourish humans." Now advising people to stop killing animals, isn't it extremely contrary to God's will?

NOTE 2

The Book of Shangshu (尚書), commonly known as the Book of Classics (書經), is one of the Four Books of Confucianism. Although the An Si Complete Book does not quote this question, it is quoted from this book.

Answer: If you know that heaven and earth are the parents that give birth to all things, why don't you know that all things are like the children of father heaven and mother earth? In a group of children where the strong one oppresses the weak, the noble one despises the poor, the

parent must be extremely unhappy. If humans eat the meat of all living things and think that heaven created them to feed them, then the tigers and leopards that eat human flesh, mosquitoes and mosquitoes that suck human blood, will they also think that heaven created humans to nurture them?

Question: Why doesn't heaven completely forbid humans from killing animals?

Answer: Heaven already has a prohibition, that's why there is a prohibition. the evil consequences of killing. But it's impossible to ban everyone, just like it's impossible to ban all species of tigers, leopards, and mosquitoes.

Question: If it weren't for heaven's creation to nourish humans, then surely species such as birds, animals, fish, turtles... should not be born. Why do we still see them breeding everywhere today?

Answer: Those animals are all born through their own karma as birds, animals, fish, turtles... If we attribute the cause of their birth to heaven, it turns out that heaven is extremely unfair. And if we say that they are born from the contrary temperaments of heaven and earth, then may I ask why only those animals receive contrary temperaments?

Question: There are many animals in this world. If everyone gave up killing and eating their flesh, they would have to multiply rapidly everywhere, and the future would become a world full of animals. What would we do then?

Answer: There are species such as earthworms, worms, snakes... humans don't catch them to eat, but we also don't see them spawning all over the world. What's more, there are many animals in this world, which is actually due to humans killing too many animals. [People who kill animals, die and become animals], the debt of killing, repaying the loan, repaying the loan, interact with each other, so they are both born into the animal world. If it continues like that, it will become the entire animal world. If everyone gives up killing, the karma of being born as an animal will gradually disappear, and there will be more and more beings born in the two heavens and humans. Looks like the people of the Chu country don't catch frogs and there are fewer and fewer frogs there, and the people of the Shu country don't eat crabs and the crabs there are increasingly rare. Isn't that clearly proven already? Moreover, today you have not yet given up killing yourself but are worried about giving birth to too many animals, compared to the story of the farmer who has not sown seeds yet but is worried that people in the world will burst their stomachs because of the surplus of rice, what's the difference?

Question: God hates killing, so it should make the flesh and blood of living beings become unpleasantly stinky, naturally no one in the world will kill anymore, wouldn't that be better?

Answer: The flesh and blood of animals is inherently stinky and unpleasant, but people eat it and think it is delicious. That has two reasons. One is due to the karma of animals, the other is due to the karma of humans, so

it turns out like that. When animals' karma has not yet been liberated, their flesh and blood bodies naturally turn into a sweet taste, tempting people to slaughter and eat. When human karma has not yet been liberated, the tongue naturally craves sweet, fatty flavors [from animal flesh and blood], finding all kinds of ways to create a life-threatening debt. If the karma of both people and animals ends, there will naturally be no more eating and swallowing the flesh and blood of living beings.

For example, if someone in his previous life was a cat and always thought about catching mice, in his previous life he was a crane and always thought about catching snakes, but since he was reborn as a human, he no longer had thoughts of catching mice or snakes. Through this, it can be seen that, depending on the karma of different life-giving bodies, there are different preferences. Different interests come from the body, different bodies come from karma, different karma comes from the mind. God cannot change people's hearts from evil to good, so how can they turn the taste of living beings' flesh and blood into an unpleasant stench?

Question: Those who take killing animals as their profession and rely on it to raise their families, now advising them to change their profession, is it like cutting off their family's way of life? That is loving animals but not loving humans, I do not accept that.

Answer: A person whose job is to kill animals is

using the flesh and blood of sentient beings to solve our hunger and thirst, although we will have food and clothing for the time being, we will have to endure suffering for thousands of lifetimes to come, which we fear will never end. It is out of pity for them that we advise them to change to another profession. If on the contrary, they think that it means ending their life path, that is truly just the short-sighted view of a narrow-minded person.

tieu_de: Doubts about not killing
noi_dung:
Doubts about not killing1

NOTE 1

This section has 8 questions and answers. (Author's note)

Question: Cattle and cows plow the fields, dogs guard the house, of course you should love them without killing them. But if goats and pigs are not used for meat, they are useless. How can they do anything else?

Answer: The reason we give up killing and saving the lives of living beings is only because we want to nurture compassion and compassion for all living beings. Is it not because of whether the animal is useful or useless? If you don't kill animals because animals are useful, it's just a selfish way of thinking for your own benefit. What's more, poisonous snakes, bats, scorpions, spiders, beetles... are all useless, may I ask why you don't eat them?

Question: Animals like chickens, dogs, buffaloes, goats... when killed, they scream in fear, so killing them would be cruel. But fish, shrimp... underwater are not at all

crying or shedding tears, how can you stop them from killing them?

Answer: The physical appearance is different from big to small, but the nature of all species is the same. For example, killing someone, whether killing a very big person like Phong Phong Thi1 or killing a small newborn child, is the same sin. If you think that a small body can kill, then humans are inherently smaller than cows and buffaloes, so killing cows and buffaloes is really not as good as killing people. It's also said that if you don't scream, you won't be in pain, so if a mute person feels pain when being killed?

NOTE 1

Phong Thi Phong: the name of a person in ancient legend, with an unusually tall body.

Question: If you personally hold a knife to slaughter, of course it will harm your compassion. But if you bring the animal to the slaughterhouse, tell the person to prepare it, then you will only take it home to eat, which is not contrary to the meaning of "gentlemen stay away from the kitchen",2 that is enough.

NOTE 2

The gentleman stays away from the kitchen: This sentence is taken from the book Mencius, the Liang Hui Wang section - the upper chapter, meaning that the gentleman, because of his kindness, cannot bear to see slaughtered animals screaming in the kitchen.

Answer: If you do that, it's just like someone covering his ears and stealing a bell [to avoid hearing the bell ringing]. If you ask someone else to kill you on your behalf, that is bringing the guilt onto that person. If we put it this way, the person who was unfairly punished with the stick should only resent the person who hit him with the stick and not resent the official who punished him unfairly. If you take an animal to another place and kill it, it can make it resent that place but not yourself. Surely a person who was unjustly exiled should only resent the land to which he was exiled and not resent the official who wrongly convicted him. But if you can deceive the animal that was killed, how can you deceive your own mind?

Question: [Speaking of releasing animals,] the animals that are released and [will later] be captured by people, what can we do?

Answer: The person who captures them is the one who captures them, the person who releases them is the one who releases them themselves. Just like a doctor treating a disease, it is impossible to guarantee that a patient will not die in the future. Or like in the year of bad harvest and famine, giving food to people, it is not possible to guarantee that they will not be hungry in the following days. Just like a builder building a big house, he cannot guarantee that it will never be damaged. In this world, everything is so impermanent and uncertain, why only doubt about releasing animals? However, when people in this world are running after fame and fortune, they are enthusiastic and enthusiastic, without any hesitation or worry. Only when faced with good things that should be done, they are timid and afraid, trying to find ways to find out what should not be done. It is no wonder that it has not created a Saha world full of suffering like this.

Answer: If the animal is hurt, you should feel even more compassion. If thanks to me buying it back and releasing it, it can live, then that merit is greater than anything else. If it is unlucky to die, it can also help it have a peaceful death. Isn't it better than having to endure the pain of being chopped into pieces and burned by boiling oil? For example, if a prisoner is imprisoned in prison, we know clearly that he is innocent so we want to save him, but because we see the image of him being dry and skinny, do we change our mind and let him fall to death?

Question: [I heard that] good deeds mainly come from the mind. If you have a good mind, then why do you need to prevent killing living things?

Answer: How can you say that? Those people who he considered "had a good heart", just because they wanted to have a delicious piece of food in their mouth, made animals endure immense pain and suffering, only to eventually swallow it through their throats and turn into dirty excrement. Thus, the cruel and evil-minded people throughout the world are no more cruel than that. Let's ask where is that so-called "good mind"? I'm just afraid that in all three evil paths1 there are only people with "good hearts" like that.

NOTE 1

That is the realms of hell, hungry ghosts and animals.

Question: Now I think there is no need to talk about whether or not you should [kill] harm], nor is it talking about the precept of killing or not precepting, just keep doing it with no mind.

Answer: If a person can mindlessly keep the precept of not killing, of course that merit is not small. But if a person carelessly kills animals, the crime is not light. Like the invaders who robbed other people's houses and shot random arrows at you, can you forgive their indifference?

Question: There are as many species of living beings as the sand in the Ganges River, now the ability to save is only limited, how can it be fulfilled?

Answer: The heavens have the virtue of loving life but do not like killing. Saving one animal is already in accordance with God's will, let alone saving many animals? For example, for a poor person, although it is impossible to have a vault of gold and mountains of silver, helping them with a measure of rice is enough to prolong their life.

tieu_de: Doubts about heavy karma are difficult to avoid
noi_dung:
Doubts about heavy karma that are difficult to avoid1

NOTE 1

This section has 6 question and answer sections. (Author's note)

Question: Animals that are slaughtered and cut into pieces [such as chickens, pigs...] were born in that situation, and it is difficult to avoid being killed. If I don't kill them, someone else will surely kill them. So what's the point of me not killing them?

Answer: The serious sins of those animals [committed in previous lives, now] are difficult to avoid being killed, but is it impossible to avoid our sins [about to be created today]? If due to [serious crime] it is impossible

avoid [of those animals] and kill them, then we and they will both suffer a serious and unavoidable sin. You should know that, because in their previous lives, those animals were also attached to the notion of "it was inevitable" [to kill living things], that is why today they have to suffer such an unavoidable sin. Why is there still a way to avoid it [that is, not committing the crime of killing them] but not thinking about it early to avoid it?

Question: The animals that are killed in life, most of them are because of [guilty in a previous life, so today they have to] pay for it, so what sin is it if we kill them?

Answer: If you commit the crime of killing, you must be reborn as an animal. Animals are killed to pay for old sins, that's natural. But people who kill animals have two cases that need to be distinguished: killing due to old debt and not killing due to old debt.

Killing due to old debt, is when the animal killed in the previous life once killed us, now the karma is ripe, the unjust family meets each other, it is right to die at our hands to repay the debt.

It's not because of old debt that we kill, it's when in a previous life someone else was killed by that animal. Now, although karma comes, we have to pay for our lives, but we don't have to pay for it.

People in the world, at a party, with meat and fish galore, on a table, hundreds of thousands of things, how can they only fall into the situation of killing because of old debt? So we must know,

if it is said that an animal is killed to repay a debt to us, then that is a very rare case, only one or two times a thousand, but falling into the situation of taking out an unjust debt on one's own and having to pay it back in the next life is almost always encountered. Speaking of this, it is truly terrifying!

Question: If you don't kill because of old debt, of course you will have to suffer retribution in the next life. But if one kills because of an old debt, one kills in the past, another kills again, it is considered that the karma of killing is ended, how can it be said to be harmful?

Answer: Don't you feel like two people are fighting? Some people fight, others fight back, then their limbs continue to take turns punching and kicking back and forth like rain. Have you ever seen one side fight over, the other side fight back and then stop, both sides let go and calmly look at each other? [Because the resentment continues like that,] Bodhisattva clearly knows the causes and conditions in future lives. Even if he meets someone who has resentment, he does not take revenge.

Question: Buddha said: "Among animals, most of them can be our parents and relatives from many previous lives." How can we prove that statement to be so cruel as to say that our grandparents and parents for many generations are now animals?

Answer: All sentient beings from countless lifetimes up to now have continuously circulated in six paths.1 Take only

NOTE 1

Six paths (six paths): include the realms of gods, humans, asuras, hell, hungry ghosts and animals. All sentient beings, due to the karma they have created, circulate in samsara and cannot go beyond these six realms.

In just one lifetime, the number of [parents and relatives] is already incalculable, [not to mention having gone through countless lifetimes,] how can it be said that all the living beings we see today have nothing to do with us? He thinks that thinking like that is cruel, but if, out of ignorance, one kills [parents, relatives from previous generations], or sees them being killed and doesn't help, isn't that cruel? That's really [exactly what Mencius said:] "Having been unable to mourn [for my parents] for three years, I now consider understanding the proper way to mourn for three months, five months."1

NOTE 1

This sentence is taken from the book Mencius, chapter Devotion, section 46. The original text is: “不能三年之喪，而緦小功之察，放飯流歠，而問無齒 決，是之謂不知務。 - The mourning of the three years of impossibility, the death of the small children; release the fan flow Xuan Nhi asked no slag decision, the position of the city did not know the fog." (You can't mourn for three years, then learn carefully about the rules for mourning for three months, five months; eat rice without even having time to chew it, and then ask about how to chew without teeth, that's called not knowing the matter.)

Question: There were so many parents and relatives in previous lives, so the number of people who fell into the animal world must be quite a lot. The only thing is, if they were my parents and relatives in a previous life, then they definitely have a predestined relationship with me, so even if they fall to the status of animals, they will not necessarily die at my hands.

Answer: Do you know that among the people who have been my parents and relatives for many generations, there are also people who came to me because of unjust family karma? When we receive a favor from someone, that person repays our old debt. When someone else receives my favor, that means I repay that person's old debt. For example, close friends

humiliation, it is true that because of good fate, we came together, so because we love too deeply, we cannot avoid being taught and scolded excessively. Continuous scolding will lead to anger, and constant anger will lead to enmity between both parties. If in this life there is a little resentment towards each other, it will surely sow the seeds for resentment in the next life. Having formed a grudge, the seeds will be planted so that the next generation will kill and devour each other. In that cycle, the strong oppress the weak, the big swallows the small, there's nothing you can't do.

You should know that the root of resentment is from relatives. If people don't have relatives, they won't have enemies. If they don't have enemies, they won't have relatives. Those who resent their loved ones are inherently treated against each other, forming the basis of reincarnation. The Tathagata teaches us to treat our enemies and relatives equally, which is truly a very subtle and mysterious teaching that can bring benefit to all living beings.

Question: Seeing someone else killing a living thing, even though you have the wish to help, but don't have the strength to do so?

Answer: [If you can't be saved, you can] quietly recite the mantra in your mind, or recite the names of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, or on behalf of that animal, develop a mind to repent, develop a mind to pray for the world, then the killed animal will naturally receive benefits.

tieu_de: Explain that entertaining guests is against the secular world
noi_dung:
Explaining how entertaining guests is contrary to worldliness1

NOTE 1

This section has 4 question and answer sections. (Author's note)

Question: When relatives come to visit, rice and vegetables are not enough to entertain; Good friends discuss together, delicious food is enough to complete the ceremony. Now, because we love animals, we give up treating them. Isn't it really wrong?

Answer: Dear friends, if they are good people, they will be happy to see that we do not kill, and will not blame us for looking down on them. If someone blames me for looking down on them because of that, they are just petty people greedy for delicious food, and it's natural for me to look down on them. Despite the serious sin of just serving food to other people's mouths, I decided not to do it.

Question: Preparing a banquet for guests is also related to etiquette. The food is so meager, is it proper?

Answer: [Confucius said:] “According to rituals, being too extravagant is not as good as being frugal.”2 Eating and drinking in excess is something a benevolent person cannot do. What is the use of being a human being without kindness and keeping the rites?3

NOTE 2

This passage is quoted from Confucius in the book Analects, chapter Eighty, section 4. In this entire sentence, Confucius talks about rituals and mourning as follows: “禮，與其奢也，寧儉。喪，與其易也，寧戚。 - Ceremony, data is far away, security is economical; funeral, data is good, time is good, security is like.” (When it comes to rituals, if it's too lavish, it's better to be frugal; when it comes to mourning, if it's too easy to ignore, it's better to be merciful.)

NOTE 3

This sentence is also inspired by the saying of Confucius in the chapter just cited above, in section 3: “人而不仁，如禮何？- Human child is inhumane, like ceremony?” (Is it possible to be a human being without kindness and to follow the rules?)

Question: People in the world compete with each other to throw luxurious banquets, I feel like they have become accustomed to the custom, even if they want to change for the better, they are alone and have no one to support them, what should they do?

Answer: Even if we don't have the ability to change people's customs, is it possible that we can't change and perfect ourselves? Throughout this world, even if we are impure, we must keep ourselves pure; Even if everyone is drunk, we still have to stay sober, only then can we be called a strong and resolute man. If you also surrender to the world and go along with others as the right way, that is just a weak style.1

NOTE 1

The original work uses “妾婦之道” (the way of concubines), referring to the behavior of servants and concubines in ancient society, doing what they are told, not daring to resist or argue. again. The author uses this meaning to contrast the strong and resolute "macho" style mentioned above. Based on the meaning, we translate it as "weak", because the original's example is no longer appropriate.

Question: If guests come to your house and specifically kill them to entertain, that must of course be avoided. But what if relatives or friends suddenly come to visit and don't have time to buy things at the market?

Answer: If you keep the precepts and do not kill, you must prepare things early in the house to treat guests. Once a guest arrives, out of fear that the reception will not be polite enough [so he thinks about being forced to kill him], it is all because he normally disregards the lives of animals. Zen Master Nguyen Van has a verse that says:

For hundreds of thousands of years, for every bowl of soup,
Resentment is as deep as the sea, hatred is as deep as a city.
If you want to know why soldiers suffer,
Look at the slaughterhouse at dawn.1

UNCTURE LIKE 1

Original Chinese text: “千百年來碗裏羹，怨深如海恨難平。欲知世上 刀兵劫 ，但聽屠門半夜聲。 - Thousand years Lai Oan Li Canh, resentment is as deep as a sea of hatred and trouble. Duc knows the world's swords and soldiers, and the disciples are sold in the night." Translation: For hundreds of thousands of years, in every bowl of [meat] soup, the resentment is as deep as the ocean, the hatred is difficult to appease. If you want to know [the cause] of war and swords in this world, listen to the cries [of animals] at the slaughterhouse in the middle of the night. – We translate the above poem based on the idea.

The person entertaining guests should write this poem and place it above their seat.

tieu_de: Explaining why killing and offering should not be done
noi_dung:
Explanation of not killing and offering2

NOTE 2

This section has 6 questions and answers. (Author's note)

Question: Sacrificing to the gods is to pray to have children, to increase longevity, or to gain fame, career, money... In the past, we used to use living things to kill to sacrifice, but now when we leave them, what can we use to show our respect?

Answer: Heaven and earth down to gods all have the virtue of loving life and hating killing. Making animals lose their children to pray for children for themselves, causing animals to shorten their lifespan to pray for their own longevity, causing animals to lose their lives to pray for fame and fortune for themselves, not to mention the fact that heaven is not forgiving, one's conscience must also see that it is cruel.

If one prays for children and gets children, that means that person is not inherently extinct. If one prays for a long life to get a long life, that means one's own life has not yet ended. Seeking fame

If you gain fame and fortune, that means that person is having a good destiny. If you do not fall into those cases, on the contrary, it is possible that the person who is about to give birth will become extinct due to the killing and it is impossible to know; Or maybe people have a long life span, but due to killing, their life span can be shortened, which is unknown; Or it is a person who inherently has good fortune and fame and fortune, but due to killing, the loss of good fortune cannot be known. That is only speaking within the scope of karma in this life, as living beings rotate in three paths, and the unjust karma of borrowing and repaying each other truly has no end date. “If you follow the worldly sentiments of the moment, you will have to suffer and pay for it in all eternity.” Isn't that sentence talking about killing for sacrifice?

Answer: When one's life span is over, neither heaven nor earth can do anything, let alone demons. Killing animals to make offerings only increases karma. If you burst out of deep love and don't know clearly about life or death, you can also offer light vegetarian food. If you listen to the heretical teachings of petty people, you will definitely want to kill living things and make offerings of flesh and blood. It is absolutely impossible.

Question: If it is a vegetarian house, vegetarian offerings are

correct. But if you eat salty food at home, use fish and meat but offer vegetarian food, isn't that disrespecting the gods?

Answer: The bird eats a rotten mouse alone, the phoenix definitely doesn't want to fight with it.

Question: The ghosts and gods enjoy sacrifices of flesh and blood, and will later fall into hell, can you believe that?

Answer: Not only ghosts and gods, even gods in the heaven of neither perception nor non-perception, when their blessings and virtues run out, they also have to receive their karmic retribution. Once upon a time, Lady Maya asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: "Why is it called the Unbroken Hell?" The Bodhisattva replied: "Regardless of whether they are male or female, dragon or god, even gods or demons, [when evil karma ripens] they all have to go there to receive retribution, so it is called Incontinence."1 When the merit of being a god has ended, it must circulate in the three paths, that is also natural.

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the Ksitigarbha Sutra. Bodhisattva. (Author's note)

Question: They are all gods, why do some enjoy sacrifices of flesh and blood, while others do not?

Answer: In my previous life, I was a righteous person, so I became a god. Among them, people with heavy anger will fall into enjoying flesh and blood, while people with loving kindness will not enjoy flesh and blood. Furthermore, because he did good deeds and gave alms in his previous life, he became a god. Among them, those who do not know the Three Jewels and only practice worldly good deeds will surely have more blessings than wisdom and will fall into the position of enjoying flesh and blood. If a person deeply believes in cause and effect and follows the Buddha's teachings, his wisdom will surpass happiness and virtue, and he will not fall into enjoying flesh and blood.

Question: If ghosts and spirits do not have the ability to influence the length of a person's lifespan, praying for a change cannot be effective. But it is true that there have been cases of serious illness where medicine was ineffective, and when they prayed to God, they were cured immediately. So, the length and shortness of human life must be decided by ghosts and gods. How can they not worship each other respectfully?

Answer: [Praying for the gods to be healed, then] the previous illness [might] have been caused by demons, but the lifespan after healing certainly cannot be extended thanks to demons. If your life span has not yet expired, even if you do not pray for reversal, your illness will still be cured. If your life span has expired, even praying for a reversal will be ineffective. It's just that he encountered evil spirits and demons, greedy for flesh and blood, and took advantage of the opportunity to harass and demand. Foolish people only see coincidences and believe without doubt. Seeing a person who prayed for the island to be cured, they thought it was thanks to the ghosts and gods that they were cured. But seeing a person who prayed for the island and still died, they thought that it was because that person did not pray for the island sooner that they had to die. Alas, I am sure that people like that will have to be born as scapegoats in the future.

The Sutra of Similes says: "Demons and spirits can know people's lifespans and sins, but they cannot save people's lives or kill people, nor can they make people rich or poor.

They just want to incite people to do bad things, commit murder, and then take advantage of people's mental weakness and mental disorder to harass them so that people can build temples and worship and worship."

tieu_de: Taking care of parents and worshiping ancestors
noi_dung:
Caring for parents and worshiping ancestors1

NOTE 1

This section has 6 question and answer sections. (Author's note)

Question: Now we know that you cannot kill an animal to sacrifice to the gods, but if you kill an animal to take care of your parents, is it a sin?

Answer: Doing so is even more serious than killing a scapegoat. As a child, the good deeds must be directed towards the parents, and the wrong deeds must be accepted by oneself. Now I don't want to kill, I just kill to take care of my parents, that is bringing evil and wrong things back to my parents. For example, with the laws of the country, if you don't dare to violate them yourself, can you make your parents violate them? When ghosts and spirits run out of blessings, they must reincarnate. Can our parents enjoy their blessings forever? If parents cannot be completely vegetarian, they can temporarily use three pure meat dishes, 2 or they can also use foods sold at markets and restaurants. If you think it is necessary to kill animals yourself to serve your parents, that is to offer poisoned wine to your parents to quench their thirst.

NOTE 2

Three pure meat dishes: are the meat of animals that fall into 3 cases: 1. The eyes cannot see when the animal is killed. 2. Ears do not hear the sound of animals screaming when they are killed. 3. There is no doubt that the animal was killed because of you.

Answer: From the perspective of a child, there are only two people who can take care of their parents. But if we consider the whole world, the number of people who are cared for is truly incalculable. If everyone killed their living creatures in order to take care of their parents, their bones would become like mountains, and their blood would flow into the ocean, wouldn't that be enough to be called a crime? By killing countless living beings like that, how can we ensure that there are no parents or relatives from many previous lives among them? Isn't it crazy to kill relatives in the previous life to take care of your parents in this life? For example, if you kill your parents in the past to take care of your parents in this life, wouldn't that be even more crazy? If it is said that killing comes from the heart of taking care of one's parents, then heaven will forgive, then ask if heaven will only forgive one person, or will it forgive people all over the world? In short, such a point of view is truly unreasonable!

Question: There is nothing more important than making offerings to a child to honor his deceased parents. When parents were born, they were not vegetarian, but now when they die, they are vegetarian. Is that not according to the parents' wishes?

Answer: If parents and ancestors rely on sacrifices to be full, then each year there are only a few offerings, so how many other days do we have to go hungry? If you don't have to go hungry on other days, you know that the offerings are just to show your children's sincerity. Can killing things that create bad karma be considered an expression of sincerity? As a child, when your parents are still alive, you cannot wholeheartedly take care of them, only making your parents have to spend a lifetime worrying and caring. After death, just because of a little vain reputation with people, it causes your parents to be involved in karma for many generations. Is that worthy of being a child? In the past, Tang Nguyen [raised his father Tang Tzu very carefully, but was also criticized for] only being able to take care of the food in his mouth, unable to follow [like Tang Tu raised his father Tang Tich, knowing how to care for] his father's wishes.1 Why do parents still live

NOTE 1

Tangzi's father (ie Zeng Sam, a student of Confucius) was Tang Tich, and Zengzi's son was Tang Yuan. When the monk took care of his father, the food tray was always neat, his father finished eating, and before serving, he always asked his father about the remaining food. The father asked if there was any more in the kitchen and he said there were still left, so once his father told him to give the leftovers to the neighbors, and he happily did so. Later, Tang Tich died, and when Tang Tu was old and weak, Tang Nguyen took care of Tang Tu, and the dinner tray was always neat, but before serving, he did not ask his father about the remaining food. The father asked if there was any more in the kitchen and he said no, intending to save the remaining food to give to his father the next day. Mencius told this story (Mencius - Ly Lau Thuong, section 19) and commented: "Taking care of your parents like Mr. Zeng Nguyen is just feeding, like Mr. Zengzi is called taking care of your father's whole heart."

make your parents suffer just because of delicious food? A filial child takes care of his parents, [even when making sacrifices] he must pray for the grain of a virtuous person,1 let alone killing an animal to put flesh and blood on a tray to make an offering, how can it be so inhumane?

NOTE 1

The Book of Rituals, Thien Te Nghia writes: "When parents die, they should pray for the grain of a virtuous person to make offerings."

Question: If descendants make sacrifices, will their ancestors return to enjoy them? Or will they not return to enjoy it?

Answer: If the ancestors are reborn as ghosts, their descendants can make offerings with the utmost sincerity and will surely return to enjoy them. If you are born in heaven and enjoy many pleasures, you will not return to enjoy them. If you fall into the three evil paths, because you are suffering, of course you will not be able to return and enjoy. If you are born in the human world, you will already have friends and relatives [in your new life], so you will not return to enjoy them. Thus, in general, although descendants are respectful in making offerings, in most cases they only enjoy those gifts themselves. These things are clearly stated in the Middle Agama Sutra.

Question: If the ancestors have not returned to enjoy, will there be other gods to enjoy?

Answer: In the Long A-ham Sutra, it is said: “In all human habitations, there are all ghosts and spirits, there is no place without them.” The Upasaka Precepts Sutra says:

Fishermen kill a lot in order to make a living, so due to the influence of karma, they have many evil relatives, just to divide their food and clothes, causing them to work hard morning and night but still not have enough to feed them, so the more children they have, the more severe their suffering. Don't you see that goats, dogs, chickens, and pigs all reproduce a lot, while the gods never reproduce? You should think carefully about that.

Question: People in life should follow the great teachings of the saints and sages, repaying the country's kindness and benefiting all people, only then can it be called precious. As for that theory of cause and effect, it has nothing to do with life or people's hearts?

Answer: The principle of cause and effect is also the way of the sages. The scriptures say: "Those who do good deeds, bestow good things; those who do evil deeds, bestow disasters." Doing good deeds or doing evil deeds, that is cause; Bestowing good things or bestowing disaster, that is the fruit.

The I Ching is called good, bad (savory), disappearing or growing (tieu tru); The Hong Pham heaven [in the Sutras] is called the five blessings (five blessings), the six tribulations (six extremes), the Vo Dat heaven [in the Sutras] is called long life (longevity) or early death (young), in Buddhism it is called cause and effect, actually it's just the same principle.

The living beings of the decadent period often indulge in bad karma, not afraid of the law, not concerned with integrity, but there are times when it is late at night. Thanh Tran suddenly thought again, in his heart he was afraid [about cause and effect] but did not dare to do bad things anymore, just because he was afraid that after death he would have to suffer retribution.

Oh, since the advent of Buddhism until now, it is impossible to know how many deranged thieves have trembled in their hearts [because of thinking about cause and effect], and how many evil and malicious people [also because of thinking about cause and effect] have been terrified. Thus, the theory of cause and effect cannot be said to not have contributed to Confucianism, helping to further the legal precepts.

If you think that good and evil deeds have no consequences, and that after death there is no need to receive

to receive punishment, then people in this world have nothing to avoid or fear. Such a view would assume that any effort to become a saint or a sage would only be in vain and suffering, but those who oppose their superiors and disrupt the rules actually get things done. So how come people in the world don't join the rebels? However, when people today discuss the morality of saints and sages, they immediately think that not mentioning cause and effect is sublime, their intentions are completely different from Taoism and Buddhism. People like that are just greedy for vanity. In fact, when it comes to the great teachings of saints and sages, they can't see anything even in their dreams.

During the Jin Dynasty, in the fourth year of the Vinh Gia era,1 the great Indian monk Buddha Do Trung came to Luoyang, saw that Thach Lac2 was a person fond of killing, so he came to teach him. Thach Lac asked: "What is effective about Buddhism?" He knew that Thach Lac did not understand anything about Buddhist teachings, so he first displayed his supernatural powers to subdue him. He held a bowl of water in his hand, burned incense and recited a mantra for a moment, then suddenly a blue lotus flower appeared in the bowl. Thach Lac was convinced. From then on, every time someone died, he immediately brought about cause and effect retribution.

Doubts about the existence of the three paths evil4

Question: Humans are the most sacred species among all things, but the matter of repaying kindness and revenge is often confusing and ambiguous. Not to mention that animals are extremely stupid, how can they know how to return kindness and gratitude [correctly]?

Answer: In the act of repaying kindness and revenge, there are things that can be considered. know, there are also things that cannot be known.

The grudges and resentments that we know to repay are cases where we can consider and know. There are also cases where people do favors that we do not know, but due to such good relationships in previous lives, today we feel joy and happiness as soon as we meet each other; Or people who have resentment that they don't know about, but due to bad fate in the past, today they naturally feel anger and hatred when they meet each other. Those are cases that cannot be known by consideration.

So, in general, the karma of killing has different results, quickly and slowly. Once the predestined karma has come, no matter whether it is heaven, humans or ghosts, it cannot escape. For example, if the person who committed the karma of killing is then reborn as a human in the future, and the person who was killed is reborn as an animal, there will certainly be things like a snake pecking, a dog biting, a tiger pouncing... If the person who killed is reborn as a human, and the person being killed is reborn as a ghost, there will definitely be things like pestilence, soul capture, sudden death, premature death... If the person who kills is born as a human, the person who is killed is born in heaven, there will be things like disasters and disabilities. illness, violent death... If the person who killed was born as a civilian, and the person who was killed was born as a mandarin, there would certainly be things like prison, shackles, unjust death convictions... If the person who killed was born as a soldier, and the person who was killed was born as a soldier, martial general, there would definitely be things like fighting with swords and spears, stray bullets and arrows flying, death in the field... If the person who killed was born in the heavens, the person who was killed was born as an asura, or vice versa. There will surely be things like mountains shaking and seas, endless fighting...

Every time people encounter disasters and tribulations, they immediately resent heaven and blame others, not knowing that each such thing has a cause, it does not come naturally.

Question: The theory of hell is just to advise people to avoid evil and do good, can it be true?

Answer: The earthly world is also true. There is prison, why doesn't it exist in the underworld? Although the Buddha advised people to do good, could he lie and deceive people? Mr. Vuong Long Thu1 said: "There are two reasons why people lie, one is to compete for benefits, the other is to avoid harm. The Buddha viewed the position of the heavenly king De Thich as a torn shoe, gold and jewels as bricks, tiles and stones, so what benefits are there to compete for? Buddha saw the sword cutting off the body as if it were drawn in nothingness, the fierce fire burning the body was just like burning an image, so is there any harm? avoid? Therefore, not only does Buddha not lie, but there is no need to lie for anything.”

NOTE 1

That is, Layman Vuong Nhat Huu, named Long Thu, lived in the Southern Song dynasty.

Once upon a time, countless lives ago, the World-Honored One was in this world as the Heavenly King of the Dao-loi heaven, named Thien Nhat Quang Minh,2 and the world

NOTE 2

Excerpted from the Compassionate Flower Sutra, volume 10, classified in the Great Chanh, belonging to Volume 3, sutra number 157. This story begins on the 17th line, page 229, sheet a. The name of this Heavenly King is Thien Nhat Quang Minh, but the An Si Complete Book writes it as Thien Nhat Quang. We base our adjustments on the scriptures.

this place was called San Ho Tri at that time. At that time, the Heavenly King looked down at the world of Jambudvipa1 and saw that everyone loved killing, so he appeared and transformed into a Yaksha ghost, coming to the place where humans asked for food. Everyone was frightened and asked what they wanted to eat. The yaksha ghost replied: "I only eat the flesh of those who kill." Then he went to the slaughterhouses, transformed into realistic-looking dolls, tore them apart and ate them. Everyone was frightened when they saw this, and they all asked to keep the precept of not killing anymore.

NOTE 1

According to the scriptures, the World-Honored One's previous incarnation from heaven saw that people in Jambudvipa love to kill, so he came down to teach and educate. The Complete Book of An Si only records that "all over the world love to kill" (killing behavior). We base our adjustments on the scriptures.

Through that story, the Buddha taught: "Although I was able to save countless sentient beings that way, due to the retribution of lying and threatening sentient beings, when I sat under the Bodhi tree and was about to attain Buddhahood, the Three Weeks demon and the demons came to terrorize me, wanting to cause me chaos and not be able to attain enlightenment. Bodhi.”2

NOTE 2

Excerpted from the Lotus Sutra of Great Compassion. (Author's comment) That is, the Bi Hoa Sutra as just quoted above. The Complete Book of An Si only summarizes and does not quote the full text of the sutra. However, there were a few incorrect details so we adjusted them based on the scriptures.

According to this story, we know that the Buddha never lied about the existence of hell.

Question: The theory about hell must be [implying suffering] right in this earthly world. Like a hungry and miserable person who has to beg for food,

not enough rice to fill, not enough clothes to wear, that is the realm of hungry ghosts. Like someone imprisoned in prison, with shackles and chains around their body, that is hell. As for the mountains of knives and forests of swords, isn't that the [suffering that] the animals being brought to slaughter have to endure? A cauldron of boiling oil, a hot furnace, isn't that exactly the [suffering that] animals being cooked and fried have to endure?

Answer: Speaking like that, it sounds like it's true, but in fact it's not. It is correct to say that in this earthly world there is suffering like hell, but it is not correct to say that hell only exists in this earthly world.

For example, people who are too lowly and stupid, people often compare them to animals, but is it possible to assume that such people are animals, and then deny that there are no real animals, which are animals with fur and horns?

Once upon a time, Sima Ongong once explained Zen verses, saying that "a gentleman is peaceful and calm, that is heaven, a petty person is often sad and worried, that is hell." Master Lien Tri strongly rebuked this understanding, saying that saying so had profound implications that would lead to the rejection of cause and effect. If what you say is true, then must everything passed down in the Classics be lies?

Question: [Let's assume] hell must be real, but it is only recorded in other books and not in

Confucian books, so Confucian students should not mention it?

Answer: If you avoid talking about hell, why not first protect your body and avoid falling into hell? If you understand the way to avoid hell, giving advice and encouragement when meeting others is also a good thing. If you don't understand, then even if you keep your mouth shut and don't mention hell, will it be of any use?

tieu_de: Doubts about vegetarianism and not eating meat
noi_dung:
Doubts about vegetarianism and not eating meat1

NOTE 1

This section has 8 question and answer sections. (Author's note)

Question: Killing living things is of course a serious sin, but eating meat seems not to be a sin, but Buddhist scriptures teach that people who eat meat must suffer evil consequences, so are the laws in the underworld too harsh?

Answer: Not only in the underworld, but The laws in this world are the same. The person who kills animals is like a robber, and the person who eats meat is like an accomplice who harbors evidence, conceals a crime, what is the difference?

The World-Honored One once told Bodhisattva Great Wisdom: "There are countless reasons why sentient beings should not eat meat. All sentient beings [revolving in samsara] should often change back and forth to be each other's parents and relatives. If sentient beings think of their parents and relatives, they should not eat meat. Flesh and blood are inherently impure and unclean, so they should not eat meat. People who eat meat Always being hated and shunned by the gods, [not receiving protection and help,] should not eat meat. Eating meat causes bad breath, so people who eat meat in their sleep often have nightmares, so people who eat meat when going into the mountains and forests can smell it [to harm their lives], so if we say that we allow [disciples] to eat meat, it is impossible that.”1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the Lankavatara Sutra. (Author's note) Similar content is found in the Mahayana Sutra Entering the Lang-gia (大乘入楞伽經), volume 6. (Mahayana Tripitaka, Volume 16, Sutra No. 672, page 623, sheet b, starting from the 3rd line). However, based on the quoted words, the Complete Book of An Si actually quoted this content from the translation of the Mausoleum Abadala Bao Kinh Hoi (楞伽阿跋多羅寶經會譯), vol. 15.) We have based on the scriptures here to adjust a few details to be more accurate.

Question: The act of dressing and enjoying this life is the result of deeds from previous lives, so people who create a lot of merit and virtue will surely enjoy a lot. Seeing that, do you know that vegetarians [don't enjoy much,] must have very little merit?

Answer: [For meat and wine dishes], enjoying it is a person with fortune, but not enjoying it is a great blessing. Therefore, vegetarians who keep the precept of not killing must see that their blessings are very profound. If we think that having food in our mouths is considered blessed, then like a chicken eating a centipede, a bird pecking at

swallowing earthworms, [food is always available,] are humans really less blessed than those animals?

Question: Now that I believe what you said, I must advise people to become vegetarians. But I would like to ask whether Confucius in the past was a vegetarian or not?

Answer: Confucius was indeed a vegetarian. The Book of Scripture says: “When fasting, you must definitely use pure food different from normal.”1 Confucius was very careful in preserving the precepts. The Book of Rites says: “Precepts are achieved from inside, manifested in external form.” Thus, Confucian books talk about this very clearly, you can verify it yourself. [Confucius also said that] those who keep their precepts pure can then communicate with the gods, while those who eat meat will have a confused and dark mind, which can be clearly seen.

NOTE 1

Actually, this sentence appears in the book Analects, chapter Huong party, 7th section, the original text is: "齊必變食，居必遷坐。 - A man will surely change his food, a resident will sit in heaven." (Maintains must change their food and accommodation to another place.) Here it means eating different vegetables and vegetarian foods than usual, and living quietly in a separate room, not having regular relations with his wife and children.

People today do absolutely nothing like Confucius in everything they do, but when they don't want to be a vegetarian, they claim that Confucius is not a vegetarian. How can they use eating meat to enter the holy gate?

Question: Confucians must inevitably base their aspirations on high and far-reaching ideals in their conduct in life. If they only insist on not drinking alcohol and eating meat, then what is the difference from the foolish men and women in the world?

Answer: The foolish men and women in this world, out of ten people, it will be difficult to find a few who know how to fast. world, where meat eaters are everywhere, how can it be said that only vegetarians are stupid, and meat eaters are not stupid? I would like to ask, from ancient times until now, among the great wicked people, have we seen any vegetarians? There really isn't. So I would like to ask, among those holding slaughter knives, to the scoundrels here and there in the market streets, do you see anyone who is vegetarian? Indeed neither. So, what is the dignity of a vegetarian, I think I can already see clearly.

Question: Being vegetarian and keeping the precepts is virtuous, now I understand, but vegetarians are often emaciated and withered, so what can we do?

Answer: The real body is important, but this temporary fake body does not need to be taken seriously.

Question: Five spicy spices also born from the earth, why abstain from eating?

Answer: That is because the taste is foul and pungent, which can hinder the practice of Bodhi. People who eat these foods are hated by the gods and stay away. Furthermore, if these dishes are eaten cooked, they stimulate lust, and if eaten raw, they increase anger and impatience. When people eat these dishes, evil spirits and hungry ghosts often come to them, sticking out their tongues and licking their lips. For these reasons, you should not eat it.

Question: Some people say that, although I am not a vegetarian, I am still better than vegetarians who break the precepts. There are others who say the opposite: Even though I am a vegetarian and break the precepts, I am still better than those who are not vegetarian at all. Please distinguish between superiority and inferiority in those cases?

Answer: It is similar to the path to fame and fortune. A person who is not a vegetarian is like a person who has never received a title. A person who is a vegetarian and then breaks the precepts is like a person who receives a title and is then deposed. If you have just become a vegetarian and have broken the precepts, it is like someone who has just been appointed to an official position and is immediately dismissed, but if you have been vegetarian for a long time then you break the precepts, just like a person who has held power for a long time and is now stripped of it and has to return to the garden.

Question: We also really want to be vegetarian, but the sweet and delicious food presented before our eyes is difficult to control, so what should we do?

Answer: If you should use the practice of contemplating the "five impure things", you will definitely be able to control yourself. What are the five things?

First is to contemplate the types of impurities. Fish and meat dishes are all flesh and blood of sentient beings, so they are not clean, they are all filthy and impure.

Second is to contemplate that the foods that animals eat are impure. The food of goats, pigs... is nothing more than bran, wine dregs, and dirty things. So how can their flesh and blood not be impure?

Third is to contemplate how impure their residence is. Those animals are in a smelly barn, defecating and urinating in the same place, extremely dirty and impure.

Fourth is to contemplate the impurity of their intestines and liver. Inside their bodies, just look closely and you will see all kinds of unclean things such as blood, pus, feces, urine, phlegm...

Fifth is to contemplate the impurity after death of those animals. Because after they are killed, the body begins to decompose and rot, and is no different from a dead body. It is truly filthy and impure.

Contemplating the five impurities like that will no longer see the desire for meat and fish dishes, but will see that a pure vegetarian diet is the right thing to do.

Question: You discuss the morality of not killing, often quoting Buddhist scriptures, it seems that Buddhist teachings are very reliable. But [according to historical records, during the Eastern Han Dynasty] So Vuong Anh2 was extremely faithful

NOTE 2

So Vuong Anh: also known as Liu Anh, was a half-brother of Han Ming De, who was appointed King of So in the land of Pengcheng (now Xuzhou in Jiangsu province). According to the story of So Vuong Anh recorded in the Book of Later Han, in the 8th year of Vinh Binh (ie 65), he once offered 30 silk cloths to atone for his sins, but Emperor Han Minh issued a decree praising him as a person who knew how to "revere Taoism, learn the benevolence of Buddha", and immediately returned all that silk to him to make offerings to the Three Jewels. Researchers often rely on this story to prove that since the first century AD, which is still very early, Buddhism has occupied an important position in the ruling class in China.

Buddhism, why is it so sinful that it brings disaster?

Answer: King So encountered disaster,1 precisely because he did not follow the Buddha's teachings. People who have turned their minds to the Buddha's door must respectfully follow the Buddha's teachings. The Buddha taught filial piety to his children and loyalty to his servants. These holy teachings are all clearly recorded in the sutras. King So was a person who believed in Buddhism and yet went against it and plotted a rebellion, so in terms of Buddhism, he was a sinner, so how could he still expect to receive blessings and help from Buddhism? Words that are not ethical, a gentleman would not even accept saying them, not to mention the Buddha is the noblest of the gods, the great saint of all the saints, how could he have privacy with a rebel?2 Short-sighted people want to rely on this to slander Buddhism, it is truly an extremely shallow and narrow knowledge.

NOTE 1

Han Minh De, who was the fourth son of Han Quang Vu De, was made crown prince, so many people were not satisfied. After ascending the throne, he secretly wanted to consolidate power and purge opponents. Around the year 70, someone falsely accused King Luu Anh of Chu of plotting treason. Although Emperor Minh knew that King So was falsely accused, he wanted to take this opportunity to destroy those suspected of opposing him, so he turned this case into a big case, involving thousands of people.

NOTE 2

According to these words of Mr. An Si, perhaps he believed that King Liu Anh of So was really plotting treason. However, most historians today agree that this was an unjust case, and Liu Ying was just an excuse for Han Ming Emperor to use it to carry out a purge to consolidate power.

Question: So Vuong Anh encountered a disaster, and now

listen to your explanation. But what about the case of Emperor Wu of Liang who worshiped Buddhism and still had to starve to death in Dai Thanh?

Answer: The story of Emperor Wu of Liang starving to death in Taicheng is just a theory of short-sighted confucianists. Now researching in the book Thong Giam,1 found a record of Hau Canh besieging Taichung, seeing Emperor Luong Vu at Tai Chi Dong Palace, his expression unchanged, Hau Canh was afraid to look up, turned around and said to Vuong Tang Quy: "There is a saying that 'the majesty of heaven is difficult to violate', I don't dare to come and look again." After that, every time Emperor Wu requested something, most of them were not granted, and the food and drinks were also limited by Hau Canh. Vuong Luan offered several hundred eggs. Emperor Wu felt bitter and asked to offer honey, but in the end there was none, Emperor Wu cried out "ha ha" several times and died.

NOTE 1

That is, the book Tu Chit Tongjian (資治通鑒), a very large history compiled by Sima Guang in the Song Dynasty, completed in 1084. The book presents an overview of a historical period of 1,362 years, from 403 BC (Warring States period) to 959 (end of the Later Zhou period). The entire work has 294 volumes, about 3 million words, in addition to 30 books of contents, 30 books of surveys (examining the similarities and differences).

[Now that we can analyze the lines recorded in history, we can know.] If the king has a bitter taste in his mouth, he must know that his stomach cannot be empty; If the king asks for honey, one can know that the king is not hungry; Saying that food and drinks are limited, one can know that it is not completely non-existent. The food in the king's house, even if it's just rice

and leftover soup, can be enough for many people to eat, is it like the fate of a slave who just cuts down on food and immediately falls into starvation? There are hundreds of chicken eggs, and there must be quite a few other things. Moreover, there are still hundreds of eggs, so how can one starve to death?

Alas, in the past, people who called themselves macho men still believed in that theory, the number was very large, but just looking at a passage in history books, we saw that they had absolutely no clear analysis, mistakenly using ears as eyes, let alone with other texts with profound meanings?

Question: After people discuss life During Emperor Wu's reign, Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty believed that if he sacrificed his life [to enter the temple] he would also abandon the whole world.1 I think that is unacceptable.

NOTE 1

In the year 527, Emperor Wu of Liang first came to "sacrifice" himself at Dong Thai Pagoda in the capital city of Kien Khang, meaning to permanently live in the temple as a monk. Bhikkhu, let go of all court and family matters. Afterwards, the court officials came to the pagoda to welcome the king back. He requested that he pay a "redemption" money to the pagoda. During his life, Emperor Wu of Liang continued to sacrifice himself to the temple many times after that.

Answer: From ancient times to the present, from foolish people to sages, there has never been anyone who did not sacrifice their life:

Three inches of breath left, all things counted,
One moment is impermanent, everything is just that.

Even though later generations laughed at Emperor Wu's sacrifice of his life, they really did not know that it was his life. My body

here has long been given up. Like himself, today he strongly believes that Emperor Wu's sacrifice of life was a mistake, not knowing that in the future there will definitely be a day when he will also have to sacrifice his life. Those who defame the Buddha will sacrifice their lives in hell, those who defame the Dharma will sacrifice themselves in the realm of hungry ghosts, those who defame the Sangha will sacrifice themselves among animals. I'm afraid that at that time, even if they wanted to sacrifice their lives at Dong Thai pagoda [like the Martial Emperor], it would not be possible.

According to the books Old Giam, Tang History, Kim thang bien,1 it is recorded that, in the first year of the Dai Thong era,2 after the construction of Dong Thai Pagoda was completed, Emperor Luong Vo personally went to the pagoda to sacrifice himself and stay in the pagoda for three days, the big and small mandarins in the court freely donated money and offerings to the pagoda. In the first year of the Middle Ages,3 Emperor Wu personally came to Dong Thai pagoda to explain the Mahaparinirvana Sutra to the masses. This time it was not the king who came to sacrifice his life. People believe that Emperor Wu sacrificed his life three times, which is wrong, and also adds the words "enslave", and thinks that the courtiers had to bring a lot of money to ransom the king out of the temple. It is inevitable that they will fall into the place of literary additions, deviations and slander.

NOTE 1

That is, the Buddhist Dharma book Kim Thang Bien (佛法金湯編) by Tam Thai Compiled in the Ming Dynasty, classified in the Van Tan Tan Tuc Kinh, Volume 87, Sutra No. 1628, a total of 16 volumes.

NOTE 2

That is the year 527.

NOTE 3

That is the year 529.

Alas, in the time of Confucius, there were no completely honest chroniclers. How can we expect the historians of the late era not to give more or less praise according to people's wishes?

Question: Regarding Emperor Wu starving to death, it must have been wrong, I now clearly understand without any doubt, but [in the sutras it is taught that] the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas all listen to the sounds of sentient beings calling for help to save suffering. Emperor Luong Vo sacrificed his life to worship Buddha Dharma. Why was he not saved when he was in trouble?

Answer: The important letting go is in the mind, not outside the body. Although Emperor Wu of Liang truly gave up his life, he did not truly let go in his heart. If you completely let go in your heart, you can throw the world away like a torn shoe. Why would you still recruit Hou Canh when you are old and plot to take over the Central Plains? Therefore, it can be known that, after three days of self-sacrifice, Emperor Wu could not help but fall into the idea of ​​​​seeking blessings, which was not entirely the intention of transcending the world. However, all his deeds such as building temples, copying sutras, and creating all kinds of merit were not in vain. Therefore, even though he encountered a traitor [Hou Canh] but still passed away at a long life, it cannot be said that it was not due to good fortune. During the Spring and Autumn period, those who hated Confucius were none more than Dao Chich and Hoan Doi, but of those two, one lived a long life, the other became an official with the position of Sima; As for those who respectfully believe in Confucius, no one is like

Nhan Uyen,1 Nhiem Ba Nguu, Tu Lo, but those three people had a short life,2 one had a serious illness, the other suffered the torture of being chopped to death.3 How should such things be explained?

NOTE 1

Tic Nhan Hui, who was highly praised by Confucius and was honored by later generations as a Demi-Saint.

NOTE 2

Tuc Nhan Hoi, died at the age of 31.

NOTE 3

The fact that Tu Lo was murdered was very tragic.

Defined karma [is the karma that has created a definite karma,] must be difficult to change, it is very clearly stated in many scriptures.4 The chaos in Dai Thanh [is determined karma,] there can be no doubt. When Zen Master Chi Cong was about to pass away, he went to the palace to say goodbye to Emperor Wu. The king was frightened, so he asked about how long and short the country's fortunes were. The Zen master did not answer, just pointed at his throat and neck, meaning to refer to Hau Canh. But Emperor Wu did not understand, so he asked again, and the Zen master immediately said: "When the old monk's tower is destroyed, your majesty's society will also be destroyed."

NOTE 4

The Mahaparinirvana Sutra distinguishes between two types of karma: fixed karma and indeterminate karma. Determined karma is karma that has all the specific predestined factors, so it must happen like that and cannot be changed. Undetermined karma is a type of karma that will happen but still depends on the influencing factors, and therefore the person receiving the karma can still make efforts to change for the better.

NOTE 5

In Chinese characters, the throat is pharynx (喉) and the neck is canh (頸), the Zen master wanted to borrow the same pronunciation to refer to the name Hau Canh (侯景), the person who was about to cause chaos.

The Zen master passed away, and Emperor Wu built an altar tower in Zhongshan for him. When completed, the king suddenly thought: "How can a wooden tower last long?" Immediately the order was given to demolish the tower and rebuild it with stone. As soon as the tower was destroyed [it had not yet had time to be rebuilt], the Hau Canh army had just arrived.1 That was an event that was determined to happen like that [so only Zen master Chi Cong could know and speak in advance].

NOTE 1

See in the Dharma Protector books. (護法論), Jin thang bien (金湯編) and Former Thong Giam (舊通鑒). (Author's note)

Question: We study Confucianism, memorize scriptures, follow Confucius, and must consider eliminating superstition as our duty. Now, why do you want to argue and defend such things?

Answer: You really don't understand what superstition is when you say that. [The word strict (端) is the starting point, the basis of the thing, the word heterodox (異) is different, so] to say superstitious (異 端) refers to things whose origin is fundamentally different from the teachings of the saints. For example, compassion is the basis of virtue, so not having compassion is superstition; Knowing shame about evil is the basis of meaning, so not knowing shame is superstition; The mind of a saint does not have four things: will, determination, effort, self,2 if these things exist, it is superstition; [Confucius once said:] "My Tao is one point that penetrates all", if it is not "one point penetrates everything", it would be superstition.

NOTE 2

This is the theory of the Confucianists of the Han and Song dynasties, saying that Confucius completely abandoned the four things (子絕四 - Tu absolute four) which are will (thoughts), qua (bias), stubbornness (obstinacy) and ego (clinging to the ego).

Tong Hieu Tong3 said: “The Five Precepts of Buddhism are the Five Permanences of Confucianism.” So, how far apart are the teachings of Confucius [compared to the Dharma of Buddha]?

NOTE 3

Song Xiaozong (1127 - 1194): 11th emperor of the Song Dynasty, ruling from 1162 to 1189.

People today do not consider this carefully, as soon as they hear about the theory of compassion, it is taught by Buddha immediately. that is, opposing that theory, causing the virtue of Confucianism to also be destroyed due to that opposition; As soon as he heard that the precepts of not stealing and not committing adultery were taught by Buddha, he immediately objected to those precepts, causing Confucian morality to also disappear due to that objection; As soon as he heard that the precept of not lying was taught by Buddha, he immediately objected to that precept, causing Confucian loyalty to be destroyed due to that objection.

Isn't that like wanting to protect Confucianism but instead harming Confucianism?

What's more, the great way of the saints and sages is always for the common good and not for personal gain. King Nghieu was respectful and often humbly humbled himself to pray for the wise;1 King Shun abandoned his own opinion and followed the will of others;2 King Vu did not boast of his own talents, did not exalt his merits; King Wen always sought to learn the unknown in morality, never stopping; Did the teachings of all of them ever contradict or criticize each other?

NOTE 1

This idea is taken from Nghieu dien, that is, the part that tells the story of King Yao in the book Thu Thu.

NOTE 2

It means being willing to accept the correct opinions of others without being stubborn about your own existing views. This sentence also has an implication from the book of Mencius, chapter Gongsun Suu, section 8: "善與人同，舍己從人，樂取於人以為善。- Good and evil are in harmony with others, let go of kindness and follow others, mocking others is good." (The goodness of yourself and others is equal, then give up your own and choose the good of others, prefer to learn the good things of others, take that as goodness.)

Mencius refuted Duong Chu and Mac Dich, that is

It is a matter of reluctance, just like the medicinal herbs rhubarb, three bean,1, good doctors only use them once in a while, not every day. If it is said that Mencius's merit [to posterity] lies entirely in refuting Duong and Mac, then without those two people, would Mencius not be worthy of honor and respect? Could it be that the fact that Mencius was worshiped and respected by future generations was due to the blessings of Duong and Mac?

NOTE 1

Rhubarb and three beans are medicines that must be used with caution because they can cause negative effects if used regularly. These two can be combined to treat dysentery and bloody diarrhea.

The Confucian family of the Song Dynasty could not really keep up with Mencius, but their hot-tempered and resentful temperament far exceeded Mencius's. People today cannot keep up with the Confucianists of the Song Dynasty, but their hot temper and resentment far exceed those of the Confucianists of the Song Dynasty. From now on, I don't know how much it will decline. Because I was afraid of that, I was forced to say these words. If people in the world understand my heart [it's good], otherwise they blame and accuse me, it's not important.

REQUIRED

tieu_de: Things that should be banned when working as an official
noi_dung:
BOOK FOUR

NICE THINGS
CAUTIONAL NOTES

Things that should be forbidden when becoming an official

A person who becomes an official thanks to many lifetimes of cultivating kindness and cultivating virtue, so today he can temporarily enjoy a glorious official title. Therefore, we must take on the responsibility of wholeheartedly loving the people and protecting all things so as not to disappoint the court's grace.

Just taking the prohibition of animal slaughter alone, it also hides many lies and deceptions that are hard to explain. In the past, the bureaucrats were often used to deceitful lies, which caused even wise superiors to often fall into the situation of being ridiculed by others.

- Mandarins encounter days such as the emperor's birthday

, holidays of the year, until days

to avoid death anniversary in the whole country,1 it is necessary to plan and issue a ban on slaughter in advance.

NOTE 1

That is, taboo on death anniversary in the royal family, like the memorial day of previous kings and queens...

- Prohibition of slaughtering buffaloes and plows, which is a ban According to royal decree

royal orders, any prince, mandarin, or all levels must strictly obey and cannot just do it perfunctorily. Therefore, as soon as he takes over as an official, it is necessary to gather all the people in the district to announce and clearly explain this ban.

- Prohibiting the butcher's house from slaughtering cattle and buffaloes is not equal to banning

a ban on all surrounding houses [not to buy and sell buffalo meat]. The surrounding houses were afraid of sin [did not dare to buy and sell], so the slaughterhouse naturally had to put down the knife.

- All kinds of buffalo skins, buffalo bones, buffalo horns, tendons

Buffalo... is only needed in the military for one or two parts, but is used in the common people up to eight or nine parts. The demand is great, there will definitely be people who secretly slaughter it. Therefore, for items that use buffalo skin, buffalo bones, buffalo horns... that can be replaced by bamboo or wood, manufacturers should be understood and encouraged to use these alternative materials.

- In times of peace, civilians should not be allowed to keep weapons like swords, swords, bows and arrows. A ban should be issued to localities, not allowed to arbitrarily manufacture, buy and sell swords, bows and arrows...

- Guard dogs and underwater animals such as

eels, frogs, turtles, snails... all kinds of things that can be completely banned from slaughtering and fishing should also be officially included in the ban.

- For service agencies in charge of investigating To arrest, must

choose talented and capable people, assign them to take turns patrolling as well as secretly investigate. If you catch a violator of the ban, you should apply a fine and use that money to reward the person who is able to catch them.

- Fishermen live precariously on boats without

place to rely on. The reason it cannot be completely banned is because current river areas impose high taxes. If we can ask the royal court to exempt taxes and encourage fishermen to clear waste land along the river, the income from the land will certainly far exceed that of catching fish and shrimp on the river. Thus, not only will it permanently end the destruction of living beings, but it will also increase land tax revenue for the country, which is a job that benefits both ways.

- Those officials who know how to cherish and sympathize with things

lives, throughout the localities under their control, in rivers and streams on the outskirts of the city, in the suburbs, should set up river sections for releasing animals and engrave stone stele inscriptions. Copy it clearly and leave it for future generations to know.

- Every year in the winter months, you should notify

local residents clearly, do not allow

prevents the flow of water to catch fish and shrimp. If river sections have been set up for animal release, it is necessary to regularly let people control them.

- When the high water has just receded, people often

build bamboo pens on the river to catch fish, not knowing that this affects the flow of the river. When there are many people setting up lanterns, the water flow will definitely slow down. If there is a sudden heavy rain, the water cannot drain in time, and the rice in the fields will suffer great damage. Therefore, during the transition period between summer and autumn, there must be daily inspections, and as soon as they are discovered, they must be destroyed immediately.

- Deep mountainous and deserted places are often places where

criminals and evildoers hide. They are often armed like the military but pretend to be hunters. If we can impose a ban on [hunting], it will protect living beings, and in fact, it will also stop their plans.

- The people who catch dogs and shoot birds are mostly

If you catch a wanderer, you should advise them to find a true job to make a living. If you don't listen to advice many times and still do it again, you should punish the crime very severely.

- Prohibiting slaughter is a good thing, don't be afraid to do it

many times, if you encounter dry weather with little rain, or on your parents' birthday, you should also apply it.

- Gods in the water on land, gentlemen

should only Respect and stay away. As a royal official, you should not come directly to burn incense to pray for the island, make offerings, or arouse the idea of ​​killing life objects [for offerings] in others. For example, if there are local people who come together to submit a petition in their name, asking to establish a temple to worship the gods and receive sacrifices with the flesh and blood of sentient beings, they definitely cannot approve.

- On days of worshiping the gods, there are often

citizens gathered together to form an association, formed a bill, [donated money,] slaughtered sacrifices, and solemnly offered prayers for the island. After the ceremony, they were filled with wine and meat, then walked in procession of the god statue around the market street, causing curious people to jostle to see and trample each other, which was really painful and angry. Local government officials should strictly prohibit this practice, don't let it become an old custom that is difficult to stop over time.

- Mediums, fortune tellers, often lie and lie

tell stories of misfortune and fortune, inciting people to pray for the island and offer sacrifices, but uneducated ordinary people strongly believe in it, so they do not dare to ignore their words, causing those who are sick to not get better, those who are not sick will soon fall into a difficult situation. poverty and need, it's always like that. The officials and parents have the virtue of filial piety, so they should use the law to punish these cases.

- Those who are loyal and filial, the people

because they build temples, are of course very praiseworthy

praise and encourage to create good customs. However, since there is a shrine, according to ancient customs, there will be two spring and autumn worship periods, so from then on, countless animals will be killed, without stopping. Is that not the will of a benevolent and virtuous person? Therefore, if a government official has the virtue of love for life, there should be a change, allowing those cases to be recorded in history books but not necessarily having to build a temple.

- Those families who have lawsuits, first of all because of the entertainment

of those in authority, do not go a day without killing animals. Therefore, the less lawsuits, the less lives lost. Therefore, officials with the virtue of love for life cannot take lightly the approval of lawsuits.
